#2023. Ronald Araujo agrees with Liverpool’s position on his £47m buy option

Liverpool would prefer to wait until the end of the season before deciding whether or not to activate Ronald Araujo’s £47m buy option.

That’s the claim coming out of SPORT, with the defender himself also understood to prefer delaying a decision until the summer.

According to the outlet in question, the Reds are thought to be “very pleased” with the Uruguayan international. However, the club is very aware of the fact that it will take a somewhat significant figure to bring the centre-back to Anfield on a permanent basis.

But barring a sudden, unexpected collapse of truly cosmic proportions, it’s difficult to see how Liverpool could manage to justify not activating the buy option come the summer.

Even if the club’s long-term plan is to use a less conservative option at right-back, the fact of the matter is they’re going to be quite short on centre-back options come the end of the season.

Club skipper Virgil van Dijk (contracted until 2027) may yet sign an extension, but we can’t see Joe Gomez staying put beyond the summer window. Either way, and even assuming that Giovanni Leoni returns from his ACL injury in excellent shape and has a significant second half of the season at L4, the Reds will need to bolster the department to the tune of potentially two bodies.

Activating Araujo’s buy option, then, feels like a necessity rather than a luxury, especially given the experience that could walk out of the door at the end of the campaign.

SPORT go on to claim that Araujo “is aware that Barcelona is keeping a close eye on him”, which doesn’t really communicate a great deal as far as intention is concerned.

Prior reporting has indicated that Barca boss Hansi Flick will hold some sway in the player’s next move this summer, but ultimately, it should be emphasised that Liverpool Football Club handed the footballer a new lease of life. Not Barcelona. And we’d like to think that’ll count for something in the long run.

#2022. “He’s Got The Yips” Mads Hermansen’s West Ham Nightmare Goes Beyond Bad Form

There is a phenomenon in sport known as the yips. It’s a condition which seems to affect previously capable sportsmen, psychologically blocking them from performing even the simplest of tasks. In darts, it can become difficult to release the dart from the hand, while in golf it can make putting almost impossible.

In essence, you’re frozen, seemingly unable to perform a task which should have become second nature. And it was during Blackburn Rovers’ second goal against West Ham yesterday, when I watched Mads Hermansen fail to dive, that I found myself wondering whether this goalkeeper has developed the footballing equivalent of the yips.

It wasn’t just that goal, of course. The first was equally concerning, when Ezra Mayers was beaten down the flank and the ball was crossed into the penalty area. The situation required some kind of intervention from Hermansen, but there was none. No punch, no parry, no save. Just indecision and a complete lack of intervention.

Unfortunately, this apparent hesitation has permeated Hermansen’s game recently and it’s hard not to conclude that he’s got the yips. There have been occasions when he has looked like little more than a bystander as goals have flown past him, sometimes appearing rooted to the spot or simply falling over rather than making a convincing attempt to save the ball.

The statistics are equally worrying. Based on the match figures we’ve examined, Hermansen has saved just 20% of the shots on target he has faced over West Ham’s last three Championship matches, conceding eight goals from ten attempts on target.

That’s an extraordinary return for a goalkeeper at any level, let alone one playing for a club with West Ham’s promotion ambitions. And while defenders must accept their share of the responsibility, the goalkeeper ultimately has to provide some resistance when opponents get a shot away.

The warning signs were already there before Cardiff, and his latest performance has only increased my concerns. I don’t know whether Hermansen is suffering from anything resembling the yips, but from watching him, I do wonder whether his confidence has deteriorated to the point where instinctive reactions are being replaced by hesitation.

This has become a huge problem, and one Scott Parker needs to address immediately. As things stand, I would have more confidence in either Alphonse Areola or Finlay Herrick than a goalkeeper who currently appears unable to make the saves West Ham desperately need.

Areola is an experienced international goalkeeper whom Parker already knows from their time together at Fulham. I thought he deserved his opportunity against Blackburn, and nothing I witnessed yesterday has changed my mind.

Hermansen’s performance was among the biggest disappointments in our Blackburn player ratings, and continuing to select him simply because he was previously considered first choice doesn’t make much sense when his performances have deteriorated so badly.

Clearly, there is a bigger issue to address in January, when West Ham will have another opportunity to examine their goalkeeping options. But we’ve only just entered November, and there are still two months and a hell of a lot of fixtures to negotiate before the transfer window opens.

That’s an awful lot of potential points to lose while waiting for a goalkeeper to rediscover his confidence. Parker has an international break in which to make some important decisions, and I would suggest the identity of his first-choice goalkeeper should be very near the top of that list.

#2021. Parker’s words prove he has so much more to offer than his predecessor | West Ham News

West Ham fans may have voiced their fury as the side slid one place further down the table after a poor run of results, but at least in Scott Parker the Hammers have a manager who understands how it really, really feels to have to witness that dross.

Unlike his predecessor Nuno Espírito Santo, Parker seems to have the ability to connect with the fan base and offer real empathy – along with hope that he will at least, work his nuts off to see a turnaround.

Nuno Espirito Santo was reduced to the same platitudes, the same apologies, but with the sense that it was just for the cameras and that he’d shrug his shoulders as soon as the interview was over, leaving someone else to fix the chaos in the dressing room and on the training pitch. West Ham’s training videos usually showed an assistant taking training, with Nuno either passive or absent entirely.

Even after a year Nuno struggled to convince fans that his ‘concern’ was heartfelt.

Parker has already surpassed his predecessor in terms of being ‘present’. Both his pronouncements and his actions – such as his first-game, half time team talk demonstrate his ability to wear his heart on his sleeve.

His words reported yesterday by footballleagueworld.co.uk do suggest, unlike his predecessor, that he’s genuinely hurting, along with the rest of us:

“Sounding somewhat hoarse after his team’s 2-1 defeat at Blackburn, Scott Parker spoke after the matchabout his disappointment at the result. Parker said that he’d talked about his team’s need to get a result from this match, even if it wasn’t playing the sort of football that he want his team to play.

He had sympathy for West Ham supporters, saying that he “wanted to get three points” for them, adding that, “What I can say is that I’m fully committed here, and I understand the pain, I understand where the fan base are.”

Parker added that he understands that the unhappiness of fans isn’t entirely a response to recent performances alone, saying that, “That’s not just this season, it’s come over a little bit of time.”

And he admitted that he was also hurting from this result: “I think everyone’s hurting here, and tonight I’m hurting because I understand that the only way we can change things is winning”

And it matters. In these dark days for the football club, mid table in the second division, leadership is what will unite team and supporters to operate together and hopefully pull the club out of its slide. Leadership doesn’t always yell, ( he’s done that too), sometimes it merely shows understanding and empathy whilst demanding better.

#2018. “We should have reacted better” | Frank admission won’t bring the points back | West Ham News

Down in ninth place, outside even the play-off places, is hardly where West Ham, the pre-season favourites and the ‘big hitters descended into the Championship’ expected to find themselves after fifteen games. This, the most competitive of leagues, throws up unexpected results each and every week and West Ham have, simply, not been up to speed.

The week after week excuses of Nuno Espírito Santo have been replaced by the emotional, heart-on-his-sleeve reassurances of an albeit shell- shocked Scott Parker, but it is clear there’s a huge challenge ahead.

Scott Parker may have a more engaging style than Nuno but excuses only count for so long

Defender Dinos Mavropanos, to his credit, takes his fair share of the blame himself for the defensive lapse that led to Blackburn’s second goal when he and his team mates switched off, anticipating a stoppage for Max Kilman’s head injury instead of playing to the whistle:

Exactly so, Dinos. However frank acceptances like this don’t bring the points back. Forget automatic promotion. Eleven points dropped in the last four games is relegation form, whichever way you look at it.

West Ham pay for the lack of competition for centre back places, as we’ve already pointed out repeatedly. Taking the blame for mistakes is one thing. Not repeating them is a whole other set of problems.

#2017. Iraola admits uncertainty over Liverpool player’s international involvement after injury scare

Andoni Iraola has expressed concern as to whether one Liverpool player will link up with his country during this month’s international break.

The Reds go into the brief pause to the season off the back of a 3-1 victory at Crystal Palace, with some of the gloss from that result removed by a questionable stoppage-time penalty for the home side and an injury scare to Dominik Szoboszlai.

The 26-year-old pulled up towards the end of the first half at Selhurst Park on Sunday and played with a knee brace after the interval until he was substituted for Trey Nyoni in the 69th minute.

After the match, Iraola admitted that the Hungarian wasn’t operating at 100% yesterday, having only recently returned from a thigh issue.

The Basque said (via liverpoolfc.com): “I don’t know [if it’s] a problem, but he definitely wasn’t 100%. Let’s see. The last thing we need now is to lose players in the international games.

“Last time, in the international break, we lost three very important players, so now I’m praying – it’s the last thing we need.

“I think he extended a little bit the knee. It was fine, but not 100%, so he has to be careful to see if he can play with the national team or not. We will see, and also hope that it doesn’t happen like the other break where we lost Alex [Isak], Cody [Gakpo] and Dom. Touch wood we are in a better place in two weeks.”

On whether Szoboszlai would link up with the Hungary squad for their upcoming UEFA Nations League fixtures, Iraola said: “I know he will do everything to go because he loves to play with the national team, but he was not 100% when he finished the game. I suppose they will have to analyse, the medical staff, and see what it is.

“I know what I want, but I also have to understand the national teams. I’m sure that Dom, if he is fine he will want to go, but I’m not sure if he’s going to be fine.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Along with Iraola, Liverpool fans with no vested interest in the Hungary national team will surely be hoping that Szoboszlai rests up during the international window rather than representing his country.

Marco Rossi’s side are away to Georgia next Saturday and at home to Northern Ireland three days later, with promotion to League A well within their grasp heading into that double header.

As captain of his country, the midfielder will no doubt be striving to play his part over the coming week or so, but there must also be a duty towards the club which pays his wages and given him a platform to reach an even higher level in his career.

Liverpool resume their season in 13 days’ time with an Anfield grudge match against Manchester United, and they still have 11 more matches to play before the end of December, so managing players’ fitness will be vital during that relentless period.

Szoboszlai has been a frustrating figure at times this term, with debate raging as to where exactly his best position is on the pitch, but his creativity came to the fore in the win over Palace on Sunday.

Also, as he’s shown on several occasions, he possesses that X-factor to conjure up show-stopping and often result-altering goals.

Whatever decisions might be taken between Liverpool and Hungary, fingers crossed that our vice-captain is back to 100% for the Man United clash on the 22nd of this month.

#2015. 'Why are you speaking? F*** off!': Kevin De Bruyne at centre of Napoli dressing room meltdown as 'divided' squad lurches towards 'disaster'... with an 'every man for himself' culture setting in at Italian giants

Published: 03:23 EST, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 05:08 EST, 6 November 2026

Kevin De Bruyne was told to 'f*** off' repeatedly during Napoli's 4-1 thrashing against Porto on Wednesday, with a dressing room crisis heating up at the club.

The Napoli squad has become increasingly fractured in recent weeks, according to the Italian media, with an 'every man for himself' culture developing into a 'disaster'.

Napoli sit eighth in Serie A under new manager Massimiliano Allegri – just two seasons after winning the title under Antonio Conte – and are near the bottom of the Champions League table after three defeats in four games.

Their cracks are showing on the pitch, with striker Lorenzo Lucca yelling at De Bruyne: 'Why are you speaking? F*** off!' during their Porto drubbing.

The pair squared up to each other and Lucca shouted his expletive command three times before they went their separate ways.

After the match, Matteo Politano told Sky Sport Italia: 'It would be nice if a few other teammates came here to give an explanation and not just us Italians, but never mind, I never hide my face.'

Kevin De Bruyne was told to 'f*** off' three times by team-mate Lorenzo Lucca during Napoli's 4-1 defeat by Porto on Wednesday

There is said to be a rift developing between Napoli's native stars and foreign players

La Gazzetta dello Sport reported that Politano was calling out Cameroonian star Frank Anguissa and Kosovan Amir Rrahmani, both two-time title winners with the club.

Politano added: 'The attitude is one that a team like ours cannot have at this level. I was not attacking anyone, we have a squad that is struggling, but we need to come together and think about this next game before the break for international duty.

'Hopefully we can recover a few players during that spell and then our season can really begin.'

There is a 'divide' between the Italian group of players and foreigners, La Gazzetta dello Sport reports, though it is mostly down to frustration with results.

Individuals such as De Bruyne, Rasmus Hojlund, and Stanislav Lobotka are more 'reserved personalities' who have reportedly not bonded as well with their team-mates away from the field.

Scott McTominay, who has an ally in fellow Scottish player Billy Gilmour, said after the Porto loss: 'Of course I’m angry.

'We lost 4-1 in the Champions League; there’s nothing to smile about. For us, it’s go on and try to figure out how to fix it.

'We’ve had a lot of injuries, a lot of important players you can’t change; attacking players as well. Let’s not beat around the bush; we’ve got a lot of injuries, and that makes a big difference whenever you come into play every three days.

Napoli have had a rough start to the season under new manager Massimiliano Allegri - despite him being a legendary coach in Italy

'So, things like these can make a huge difference for the team when the same players are playing over and over again. People need to understand that, but we also need to do better. First and foremost, we need to do better, injuries in football are part of it, but we have too many.'

Their dressing room troubles have dragged on for a while. Last season, Conte complained of a lack of unity after they signed nine players on the back of their Scudetto. They still managed to finish second, but it was a turbulent ride.

'Nine new players were too many. We weren't balanced,' he said at the time.

'I experience the dressing room every day, so I say certain things; we mustn't despair. We'll try to recreate last year's chemistry.'

In one match against AC Milan, De Bruyne threw a tantrum after being subbed off by Conte.

#2014. Nils Koppen deserves credit as West Ham ‘dodged huge summer transfer bullet’

There is a tendency to lump every player together in a failing team and declare them all unfit for purpose, as the West Ham fans’ much publicised chanting at Ewood Park might suggest. However, the boiling over of a couple of years of frustration and anger, aimed at the current occupants of the claret and blue shirts, need not be taken as voicing disapproval of the whole squad.

In fact, there are some positive signs – Ezra Mayers, as we wrote elsewhere this morning- gives us all cause for optimism.

I’d wager that another starter against Blackburn, Edvin Austbø is perhaps wondering about now what kind of hell he has signed up for as one of the Hammers’ youngest summer recruits.

However his is another fledgling career that looks to be hugely promising. Against Blackburn, the young winger looked prepared to take on and beat players in a way that his more seasoned colleague Manor Solomon appears to have forgotten.

Remember, West Ham were linked with Stoke City’s winger  Sorba Thomas in the summer – an ex Hammer who has in fact gone to Premier League Hull City and struggled enormously – so much so that footballleagueworld.co.uk claim ‘West Ham dodged huge £10.5 million transfer bullet’:

West Ham made a pretty shrewd decision by backing away from Sorba Thomas and investing in Edvin Austø

We may think things are bad right now, but with youngster Austbo West Ham look to have found a young talent with a high ceiling – compared with the -relatively speaking – wizened old pro’ Thomas who at 27 seems to have peaked, if Hull City’s experience is anything to go by. Good choice, Nils Koppen.

Very easy to hate on all things West Ham just now with the club sitting outside even the play off places. Austbø however continues to shine even on dark days at Ewood Park and needs to be nailed-on as a starter in place of Solomon who, by comparison, just looked plain ordinary.

From the old Bobby Moore Upper to the Billy Bonds' stand these days - I've been watching since '03 and a supporter since about 1970.. Favourite player - Dean Ashton: Curse you Shaun Wright-Phillips. I still watch YouTube repeats of the Cup Final of 2006 hoping in vain that Shaka Hislop grows another six inches and stops Steven Gerrard's injury time equaliser. Can tell I'm getting old knowing I watched both Mark Noble's debut and his last game at West Ham. Pulling on a Claret and Blue replica shirt still makes me feel the same butterflies as when I was seven years old. Magic.

The fans are the ones who are a credit to our club Weve proved our loyalty time and time again Waiting to see it from management owners and players

Credit for signing a player who has done what exactly in the second division so far? £20M on Engles, £5m on Solomon and £10m for Piroe had we gone up? I see nothing here to give him credit for. I was chatting to a guy Saturday who told me he thinks West Ham are the easiest team to play through in the league. He reckoned our midfield had zero defensive qualities and constantly left our back four exposed. The more I think about it, the more I see what he is saying. If we had no intention of playing Alvarez or Magassa, why didn’t we sign a midfielder who can defend or tackle because none of the current bunch can.

Promotion has to be the key aim this season, but it was always going to be a reset after the torrid few seasons and incompetent leadership at the club under Sullivan and his managers. I was ok with Nuno staying on, but hindsight always being clear 20/20 vision, I think it was Paco Jémez that was the factor in West Ham’s improvement towards the back end of last season. I hope Parker brings the feelgood factor back to the squad, last seen during the high times of Moyse. Stating the bleeding obvious, there’s still time to push for that automatic spot, but no room now for what we’ve been witnessing recently if it’s going to happen for us.

#2013. Newcastle’s limitations exposed by Bournemouth before hosts fight back for draw

This was the definition of a hard-earned point. Newcastle United came back from two goals down to rescue a point against Bournemouth, but this was not a convincing performance from Matthias Jaissle’s side.

Newcastle were abject for the first half an hour and the visitors could have been out of sight. It was disjointed and lacklustre as Bournemouth dominated before the break and regularly threatened Lukasz Hornicek in goal.

Even during the fightback, Newcastle lacked cohesion and penetration, but forced their way back into it through hard work, spirit and determination. Whether you believe Harvey Barnes’ wonder goal and Jacob Ramsey’s late strike paper over the cracks or reveal a togetherness – a grit and determination that bodes well for the future – depends on the individual.

Ramsey comes off the bench to fire Newcastle level! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UBWAfCQyy4

For the second weekend in a row, Newcastle had just two shots on target and scored two goals. At the other end of the pitch, they have allowed their opponents 61 shots in just three games, the highest in the division. That is not going to be sustainable long term. Something Jaissle acknowledged.

“It shows where we have potential,” he said. “There are elements to improve offensively.

“The learning curve is there. There were some elements missing from our performance but there was a strong response. The lads showed big character, big personality and big commitment... It is always better to get a point and see the potential to improve.”

A reality check is not necessarily a bad thing. There has been a lot of hype and excitement on Tyneside and a self-congratulating tone to their own end of summer appraisals.

But this was a reminder of the team’s limitations and the fact that only three of their eight summer signings started the game, with two more coming off the bench, underlined they are a work in progress.

In truth, that is fine. It is the start of September and the Premier League campaign is only three games old. They have a new manager and a new-look team. There has been a significant amount of change in a very short period of time.

It was not the easiest summer, and despite the insistence from senior figures at the club that they had always remained calm and methodical during their summer reset, there was a whiff of crisis only a few weeks ago.

When Eddie Howe quit as manager and Bruno Guimarães, the captain, forced his move to Arsenal at the start of August, Newcastle looked in disarray. So, to have started the season unbeaten from three games against Liverpool, Tottenham Hotspur and Bournemouth is encouraging.

It is also worth highlighting just how good the visitors were. In the first half Bournemouth were superb, rushing Newcastle, forcing mistakes and pouring forward in numbers. In Alex Scott, just as he was in their victory here last season, Bournemouth had the best player on the pitch.

That opens up another conversation. Newcastle played like this a lot at home in Howe’s final season in charge, especially in the second-half of the campaign, but tended to lose not draw the game.

On this occasion, they secured a decent point with a late equaliser thanks to substitute Ramsey, who looked good when he replaced the off-colour Lewis Miley.

Bournemouth will feel they should have held on. They had taken a deserved lead through Marcus Tavernier, who took advantage of a static and ball-watching Amar Dedić to bundle home from close range.

Tavernier gives Bournemouth the lead at St James' Park! 🍒🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/mDdb5uV4hj

Marco Rose’s side should have scored again minutes later when Sven Botman gifted the ball to Evanilson on the edge of the Newcastle area, but he failed to hit the target.

Bournemouth had their tails up and when another blunder from Dedic – galloping forward and losing possession with a heavy touch – Nico González, another new signing, failed to make a tackle to stop the attack.

Justin Kluivert’s long-range strike thumped against the post and hit the back of goalkeeper Lukasz Hornicek. Scott reacted quickest and his cross spun into his own net off the leg of Malick Thiaw.

Bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39

Newcastle were in disarray and were lucky to be back in the game before half-time as Barnes whipped in a stunning strike 25 seconds after the restart.

Bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39

Despite seeing more of the ball, other than a Joe Willock header that dropped wide of the post early in the second half, Newcastle did not create another clear goal-scoring opportunity until Ramsey’s equaliser.

That is a cause for concern, but Newcastle remain unbeaten. Nothing shapes perceptions more than results. Jaissle is right to cling to the positives from that.

Speaking to TNT Sports, the Newcastle boss said: “Mixed feelings. Happy for that spirit, that belief the lads were showing until the end together with the crowd. I felt the energy and felt if we had five or 10 minutes more we could win this game. But the first half was not expected. This is something we need to improve. This is part of the journey.

“We knew Bournemouth would come with everything, they always show great intensity and if you do not compete with that you get problems. We struggled with that in the first half but the lads showed the right reaction.”

Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of this Saturday lunchtime fixture between Newcastle United and Bournemouth at St James’ Park.

The hosts have made a determined start to the 2025-26 season under new head coach Matthias Jaissle. They conceded a last-minute penalty to draw 2-2 with Liverpool on the opening weekend of the Premier League campaign, sealed a hard-fought 3-2 victory over West Bromwich Albion in the Carabao Cup, and then produced an inspired second-half performance to win 2-0 away at Tottenham in their previous top-flight outing.

Despite anxiety in the summer after losing Eddie Howe and multiple key players such as Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon, the Jaissle era has begun very encouragingly. New signings including Lukas Hornicek, Amar Dedic and Nico Gonzalez have seamlessly slotted into the starting XI, Lewis Hall has been typically brilliant, while Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa look reborn up top after both forwards endured difficult campaigns last season.

Marco Rose’s Bournemouth tenure has started in frustrating circumstances. They had been leading 1-0 against Manchester City in their first top-flight fixture this campaign, but conceded two late goals to dramatically lose 2-1. Bournemouth were also left kicking themselves last weekend against Everton, after a defensive mix-up between Ryan Christie and Marcus Tavernier following a corner delivery gifted James Tarkowski a 91st-minute equaliser, allowing the visitors to salvage a 1-1 draw at the Vitality Stadium.

At opposite ends of the country, over 350 miles separate these two sides. Away days in English football can’t really get any longer. The travelling Bournemouth support will hope their loyalty can be repaid with a first Premier League win of the season under Rose, while Newcastle will aim to continue their unbeaten start and carry on the positive momentum created by Jaissle.

Kick-off is at 12:30, with team news coming shortly.

#2012. Scott Parker Has a Selection Dilemma and the Numbers Are Damning

Plenty has already been written about Mads Hermansen, with transfer speculation continuing to swirl. Reports suggest Newcastle’s Nick Pope could be a target when the January window opens, but for now, West Ham’s goalkeeping situation remains firmly under the spotlight.

The numbers are difficult to ignore. A goalkeeper who isn’t making enough saves and is shipping goals at an alarming rate, 23 conceded in 15 games, is becoming a problem that cannot be overlooked.

One possible solution could be Alphonse Areola, who previously worked under Scott Parker at Fulham. There is also a potential opportunity for highly-rated youngster Finlay Herrick, who may be worth a closer look.

While Areola’s statistics last season hardly inspire confidence, conceding 37 goals in 20 appearances without recording a clean sheet, there is at least some context. By comparison, Hermansen managed seven clean sheets while conceding 28 goals in 18 matches.

The pair offer very different strengths and weaknesses! Areola is arguably the better shot-stopper but struggles when asked to play out from the back. Hermansen, meanwhile, has been preferred for his distribution and comfort in possession, yet questions remain over his save percentage and ability to keep the ball out of the net when it matters most.

Ex-Goalie Nuno failed to get the best out of Hermansen

Another concern is the absence of an established senior goalkeeping coach. That said, it’s worth remembering that the club’s former manager was a goalkeeper himself, while Rui Barbosa brought years of coaching and playing experience. Neither appeared able to significantly influence Hermansen’s development.

Currently, Billy Lepine, a former Dagenham & Redbridge youth player who has worked within the academy setup since 2008, occupies the role. Lukasz Fabianski is also assisting on a part-time basis with the academy.

And perhaps that’s where the story takes an even stranger twist.

Cast your mind back to 4th December 2024, when West Ham travelled to the King Power Stadium. Leicester won 3-1, ending a six-game winless run. On that night, West Ham peppered the Leicester goal with 31 shots, the highest number they had ever recorded in a Premier League match. Ten were on target and they dominated possession with 61%.

Standing between the posts for Leicester that evening?

None other than Mads Hermansen, who produced a performance worthy of Middle-earth, adopting Gandalf’s famous stance of “You shall not pass!” as he admirably defended his goal.

The previous year in the Championship he featured in the EFL team of the season. One of the most proactive ball playing keepers in the league, and completed 13 clean sheets.

If ever there was evidence of the “West Ham goalkeeper curse”, that might just be it.

The solution feels fairly straightforward. Bring Fabianski into the senior goalkeeping coaching setup, get Areola focused solely on football rather than the DJ decks, and bring in an experienced goalkeeper on loan in January to provide competition.

The ball is now firmly in Scott Parker’s court.

I have been a season ticket holder since the late eighties, so experienced the highs and lows of being a West Ham supporter. I previously wrote for OLAS and have contributed to a number of football publications in the past.

Middle of the park a bigger issue than front and back of the team

A top goalkeeper and a striker should be our priority in January

Now I am not saying Hermansen shouldn’t be relieved of his duties — he should be replaced.

However, last season’s Stats shout out what problems our Goalkeepers face ….. Areloa played his matches with Dinos and Dumbo, whoops sorry, Kilman in front if him, whilst tge majority of Hermansen’s matches had Dinos and Disasi.

Replace Kilman and whichever goalkeeper is in between the Hammers sticjs, will have improved Stats

Does Fabianski still have his boots and gloves? Seriously Herrick is much better at playing out from the back than the other two, he just seems lacking in height for me. Would he dominate his area in a way we have been calling out for this season?

Our “goalkeeper curse” is nothing compared to our “striker curse”.

#2010. Alexis Mac Allister shares what one Crystal Palace player told him about Alisson on Sunday

Alisson Becker’s outstanding performance in Liverpool’s 3-1 win away to Crystal Palace on Sunday was reflected in what one Eagles player told Alexis Mac Allister.

The Reds’ number 1 had shipped criticism in recent days for errors in the defeats to Arsenal and Fenerbahce, but he was back to his world-class best at Selhurst Park yesterday as he turned in a man-of-the-match display for his side.

The Brazilian pulled off six saves in total against Pierre Sage’s team, including a stunning reaction stop to keep out a fearsome volley from Daichi Kamada just a couple of minutes before the Argentine scored the visitors’ opening goal.

Speaking to BBC Sport after the match (via liverpoolfc.com), Mac Allister was singing Alisson’s praises and shared what the Japan international had told him about the Liverpool goalkeeper.

The Reds’ number 10 said of the Brazil stopper: “He’s so good, especially the save from Kamada’s shot [in the first half]. Kamada couldn’t believe the save he made and he was telling me, but that’s who he is.

“He is an amazing goalkeeper and an amazing guy as well. I’m really, really happy for him.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Alisson had endured some unusually shaky moments in recent weeks, but he reminded us all on Sunday that class is permanent and that he remains pivotal to Liverpool’s hopes of success this season.

In addition to the outstanding save from Kamada, he also produced excellent stops to keep out an Adam Wharton header just before half-time and a double save from Yeremy Pino and Jefferson Lerma in the 77th minute when the Reds were 2-0 to the good.

That Palace scored just once from an xG of 2.6 yesterday sums up just how imperious our number 1 had been, and it’s no wonder that the Eagles’ Japanese attacker was stunned by the 34-year-old’s brilliance.

Such was Alisson’s performance at Selhurst Park that the Premier League’s official X profile posted a compilation of his saves from the win over the south London outfit, with the goalkeeper treating us to his own showreel.

Anyone who might’ve thought that the Brazil international was in irreversible decline was made to think again yesterday by a masterclass from Liverpool’s legendary number 1.

#2007. Australian football rocked by allegations players fixed matches and illegally bet on their own games

Published: 05:28 EST, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 05:28 EST, 6 November 2026

Football Australia is investigating allegations that players registered with an Adelaide soccer club manipulated matches and illegally gambled on their own games during the 2026 season.

The Cove FC has responded to the reports by stating the club itself is not under investigation, and that the allegations concern 'a very small number of individuals' registered with the club.

The Trott Park club, in Adelaide's southern suburbs, released a statement on Friday after reports emerged of the integrity probe.

Football SA has confirmed an investigation involving players registered with Cove during the 2026 season, with Football Australia handling the matter.

'The Club wishes to make clear that The Cove FC itself is not under investigation,' chairman Phil Hole said in the statement.

'The allegations concern a very small number of individuals registered with the Club during the 2026 season.'

Players registered with The Cove FC during the 2026 season are the subject of an ongoing Football Australia integrity investigation

The probe reportedly concerns allegations of match-fixing and illegal betting on players' own games

According to News Corp, the allegations involve competition manipulation and illegal betting on the players' own matches.

No individuals or specific fixtures have been publicly identified in the supplied statements, and no findings or penalties have been announced.

Football Australia told 10 News Adelaide that its disciplinary process was ongoing and it would not comment further while its integrity unit worked through the matter.

Hole said Cove had cooperated with the national governing body throughout the investigation.

'The Cove FC takes matters of sporting integrity extremely seriously and has cooperated promptly and fully with Football Australia since becoming aware of the allegations and throughout the investigative process,' he said.

'The Club respects the ongoing investigative process and will not comment further at this stage.'

Football SA said Football Australia had exclusive jurisdiction to investigate the alleged integrity breaches, and that the state body would assist if requested.

'Cove FC have been fully cooperative and supportive of the investigation by Football Australia,' Football SA said.

Chairman Phil Hole says Cove has cooperated fully with Football Australia throughout the investigative process

'While the investigation remains active, Football SA is unable to provide details about the allegations or the parties involved.'

Daily Mail has contacted South Australian Police for comment.

Founded in 1983, Cove operates from the Southern Soccer Facility at Trott Park and has more than 800 members.

Its senior teams compete at semi-professional level, while the club also provides junior, women's, amateur, masters and inclusive football programs.

Hole said the club remained focused on its members and community while the investigation continued.

'We remain firmly committed to the values, standards and sporting integrity that underpin our Club,' he said.

'Our focus remains on our members, our community and building on the positive progress and success of The Cove FC.'

Strikers, you would think, tend to have longer careers than wingers. One player could give Liverpool ‘a chance’ of being involved in the Premier League title race this season if he stays ‘fit and available’.

That’s according to Troy Deeney, who made such claims about Alexis Mac Allister after another standout performance from the midfielder in the Reds’ 3-1 victory over Crystal Palace on Sunday.

The Argentine opened the scoring with a close-range header shortly before half-time, taking his goal tally for the season to five and matching his haul from the entirety of 2025/26.

Despite the 27-year-old’s consistently top-class displays, he’s yet to be offered a new contract by Liverpool, a situation which has baffled Deeney.

The former Watford striker selected Mac Allister in his Premier League team of the week for BBC Sport, outlining: ‘How this guy has not got a new deal I don’t know. He keeps coming up big, high energy, and he is vitally important to the way Liverpool play.

The World Cup winner was one of the Reds’ biggest disappointments in a chastening 2025/26 season for the club, but he’s been among the standout performers for his team since Andoni Iraola took the reins from Arne Slot over the summer.

Not only is Mac Allister chipping in with a steady supply of goals, he also showed his commitment to the cause and to his teammates by confronting Jefferson Lerma in the closing stages when the Palace player got involved in a spat with young Trey Nyoni.

With a gap of nine points to make up on leaders Arsenal, it’ll take a remarkable level of consistency from Liverpool to haul themselves into genuine title contention going into the latter weeks of the campaign.

Could our number 10 potentially elevate us into the title picture if he maintains this standard of performance? In truth it’ll require the rest of his teammates to follow suit, rather than being overly depending on just one or two individuals.

For now, though, Mac Allister just needs to keep up what he’s been doing since August and mind the disciplinary tightrope – he’s one yellow card away from a suspension in the Premier League, and two in the Champions League.

On current form, Liverpool can’t afford to be without the Argentine for long.

#2002. Confession shows former favourite’s love affair with West Ham continues from afar

It has taken three years for West Ham to spiral from the summit of their footballing prowess to the depths of second division mediocrity, and the Hammers’ experiences can serve as a cautionary tale to any other poorly run Premier League side. Hammers fans have also taken years to process the sale of their most successful captain since Billy Bonds, the Chairman announcing his availability the very day after their Europa Conference League trophy sale. For that alone, I’ll never forgive Sullivan.

There are ways of doing things. and that isn’t it.

As supporters we are now getting used to seeing Declan Rice in an Arsenal kit, and for many – most, I’d guess, but not all.. there’s a vicarious sense of pride still for the former Hammer, although of course not his club, as he goes onto deserved success.

It is clear the players’ love for West Ham hasn’t diminished either. Speaking to GQ magazine, Declan professed:

““I obviously love West Ham so much still, still a massive part of my life, I still watch them.”

Picking out his favourite goal ever, Rice glossed over those Champions League free kicks and confessed a goal in Claret and Blue meant more to him:

“My favourite goal is when I was playing for West Ham in the Conference League,” Rice said. “I picked the ball up on the edge of our own box and ran the whole pitch. As I was running forward I just remember the stadium getting louder and louder and louder, and as I scored the goal the place just erupted.

So I think that was one of my best solo goals.”

How fast and how much things have changed in the ensuing three years.  The only comfort for West Ham fans is that they can change back again just as fast. COYI!

#2000. Mum rushes to goalkeeper in Spanish football's killer collision: Jesus Owono suffering 'hardest days of his life' and being comforted after striker he clashed with died from 'chest trauma'

Published: 05:24 EST, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 05:29 EST, 6 November 2026

Goalkeeper Jesus Owono's doting mum has rushed to Andorra to comfort him as he endures the 'hardest days of his life' following his death clash with a rival striker whose funeral took place yesterday.

Maria del Carmen Owono Mangue made the five-and-a-half-hour drive from her home in the Basque city of San Sebastian to Andorra where her 25-year-old son currently plays his football after learning Jesus de Miguel had lost his fight for life in a Tenerife hospital.

She and the Andorra FC keeper have been deeply close since he moved to San Sebastian from their native Equatorial Guinea as an eight-year-old boy to rejoin her after she had emigrated earlier in search of work to provide for her family and an aunt had taken the youngster into her home.

Owono, the eldest of six siblings, has admitted of his arrival in a new country: 'I came in pursuit of a dream, not the dream of playing football, but the dream of being with my mother.'

His mum has confessed: 'Waking up in the morning and seeing your child doing what they love most is a mother's greatest joy.'

She said in the same interview when the goalkeeper was just 20 in comments which could now come back to haunt the family: 'He needs to keep working. We still don't know what will happen. If God allows things to turn out well for him and if not, well, you know that he has worked hard and done what he could.'

Goalkeeper Jesus Owono is suffering and being comforted after his killer collision

Owono, who has closed his social media accounts, has had his mother rush to his side in the days following Jesus de Miguel's death (Source: Instagram)

Overnight one of Jesus' younger brothers confirmed their mum was by his side in Andorra.

Speaking from the second-floor four-bed apartment she owns in a tree-lined street in a middle-class residential neighbourhood east of San Sebastian's city centre, he said: 'We're all very distraught. My mum has gone to be with Jesus because he is suffering.'

A source close to the goalkeeper added: 'Maria del Carmen is one of the most important, if not the most important, people in Jesus' life.

'He had a difficult start being separated from his mum at such an early age and it was very difficult for her too.

'They have been inseparable since Jesus moved to Spain as an eight-year-old.

'Maria del Carmen has helped him integrate into completely new surroundings and supported him every step of the way on his road to becoming a professional footballer.

De Miguel and Owono collided - and hours later the former died of 'accidental chest trauma'

De Miguel's team-mates are pictured arriving at his funeral in Navahermosa on Thursday

'It's only natural that she'd want to be by his side now when by his own admission he's in pieces and finding it impossible to come to terms with the fact a fellow footballer has died because of something he did.'

From the FC Andorra supporters' section, we want to send you all our support and love during these tough and difficult times.

We are aware of the suffering you are going through after what happened. We know these aren't easy days, but we want you to remember one thing: you are not alone.

You have your family, your friends, your team-mates, the staff, and the entire club by your side. But you also have us, a fanbase that appreciates you, respects you, and today, more than ever, wants to send you all our love and support.

We also want you to know that we categorically reject all the insults, threats, and judgments you've been receiving lately. An accident doesn't define a person, much less their character.

We don't want the pain, anger, or helplessness to turn into hatred towards you. Behind the footballer is a person, with feelings and a family who are also suffering.

We want you to know that this is your home. When you return to the pitch, to defend our goal and wear this jersey again, you'll have a stand that will still be by your side, cheering you on as always.

Now you don't have to prove anything to anyone. It won't be easy and it will take time, but even though it's difficult and painful, we have to move forward, we have to work to recover that fighting spirit and smile that are so characteristic of you. The most important thing now is your recovery, but along the way, know that you can count on us, that you're not alone.

Stay strong, Jesus. We're with you. Our Spider Man today, tomorrow, and always.

Some of Owono's Andorra FC team-mates and members of the club's supporters' group have also paid him a visit to deliver a letter of encouragement.

The letter refers to the goalkeeper as 'their Spiderman,' 'his joy,' and 'a person with feelings and a strong family connection.'

Owono was red-carded after kneeing the 30-year-old CD Tenerife striker in the chest in a reckless tackle late into stoppage time during a second-division match on Monday.

The match was suspended when the two sides were drawing 2-2.

Tragic Jesus, whose partner Marta Fernandez and one-year-old daughter Carla were watching from the stands, was reportedly revived by paramedics on the pitch after going into cardiac arrest before being rushed to hospital.

His club confirmed around 9.30am local time on Tuesday he had died about 8am the same day, saying they were 'heartbroken' and had a 'lump in their throats' after revealing earlier the footballer's neurological condition had worsened.

A post-mortem concluded in a preliminary report his death was consistent with 'accidental chest trauma' although the results of further tests conducted during the autopsy are still pending.

Owono used 'excessive force' while contesting the ball near the half-way line according to the match referee's report.

He is facing a lengthy ban and possible criminal charges after police in Tenerife confirmed homicide squad officers were looking into whether had committed an involuntary manslaughter.

Legal experts have cast doubt on the possibility of prosecution because the clash that resulted in Jesus de Miguel's death occurred during open play.

The first photos of the dead footballer's partner emerged overnight as his team-mates prepared to travel to the small town of Navahermosa, 80 miles south-west of Madrid, where his devastated parents come from.

Jesus' mum and dad made the return trip after jetting to Tenerife to try to reach their son before he died in hospital on Tuesday morning hours after his clash with Owono.

The father was watching the match in a bar in his home town when he saw him slump to the ground.

Equatorial Guinea international Owono, who turned round as he headed back to the dressing rooms following his sending off and walked back to the player he had hurt after realising how seriously injured the Tenerife frontman was, broke his silence on Wednesday.

The father of De Miguel, is hugged at his son's wake, three days on from his death

The football world has rallied behind De Miguel and his family with tributes to the striker

A neighbour said De Miguel's father (pictured right, with his mother, girlfriend and sister R-L) burst into tears after seeing the impact of the collision on television. (Source: Instagram/martitamig)

He released a statement via his club that said: 'These are the most difficult days of my life.

'I am struggling to find the words, and it is very hard for me to process anything that has happened.

'I feel immense pain over the loss of Jesus. I am thinking of him, his family, and all the people who loved him.

'I know there will be many matters to address, and I will face whatever comes with complete respect.

'But right now, honestly, I cannot think of anything other than Jesus and the grief we are experiencing. Rest in peace, Jesus.'

FC Andorra, reacting to news of the Tenerife striker's death in hospital, said on Tuesday morning: 'Heartbroken and devastated, we wish to extend our deepest condolences to the family of Jesus de Miguel, all his colleagues and friends, and to CD Tenerife.

The Hungarian FA has issued an update on the fitness of Dominik Szoboszlai ahead of their upcoming UEFA Nations League fixtures.

There is an injury concern over the midfielder after he sprained his knee in Liverpool’s 3-1 victory over Crystal Palace on Sunday, with Andoni Iraola unsure as to whether or not the 26-year-old would be able to represent his country during this international window.

The Magyars are away to Georgia this coming Saturday and then host Northern Ireland three days later in what could be a straight shootout for promotion to League A on the final matchday.

On Tuesday, the Hungarian FA published an update via X in which they confirmed that a decision on Szoboszlai won’t be taken until the latest possible opportunity.

They stated: ‘Dominik Szoboszlai has undergone the required medical examinations. Following his knee sprain, the national team’s medical staff will do everything possible over the coming days to ensure that the team captain is available to the coaching staff as soon as possible.

‘However, a decision on his availability for the match will almost certainly only be made at the last minute.’

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

As captain of his country, the 26-year-old will no doubt be striving to prove his fitness in time for the match against Georgia on Saturday, or at least be in a position to play against Northern Ireland.

However, those of a Liverpool perspective will surely be hoping that Szoboszlai isn’t risked in either game if he isn’t 100% fit to feature, as he’ll be very much needed at Anfield going into the unforgiving winter schedule.

The Reds still have 11 more matches to play in 2026, starting with a grudge fixture at home to Manchester United on Sunday week, and squad depth and rotation will be essential during that hectic period in the run-up to Christmas and New Year’s.

Whatever the decision on Szoboszlai might be in the coming days, fingers crossed that he’ll be fully fit and firing in time for the Red Devils’ visit to Anfield in 12 days’ time.

#1993. Why Enzo Maresca is sticking with 'awe-inspiring' Gianluigi Donnarumma despite Leipzig horror show, growing catalogue of errors and a worrying downward trend

There was a Manchester City fan on Thursday’s Ryanair flight back home from Leipzig wearing a Gianluigi Donnarumma sticker on his coat, portraying the Italian as Don Vito Corleone. The sticker, a bit worn and a bit crumpled, was peeling off. A metaphor exists within that somewhere.

Tough times for Donnarumma, a calamitous night in the Champions League – beaten at his near post by Ridle Baku's cross for one goal, fumbling another routine effort at the feet of a striker and allowing a straightforward shot to squirm through his fingers – just adding to the feeling that the past few weeks have not reflected kindly on him.

Question marks around Donnarumma’s suitability between the sticks are becoming more pronounced after a catalogue of mistakes this season. One against Paris Saint-Germain when Maghnes Akliouche’s shot was too hot (some would argue two after neglecting his near post for Desire Doue’s opener) and then Nicolas Jackson shooting through him at Aston Villa last month.

Each time, Enzo Maresca has publicly recognised the errors and intimated that nobody needs to rake over them in detail with his No1, who is experienced enough to know he must do better.

Now Leipzig. ‘It’s not a concern,’ Maresca said of the latest gaffe. The manager’s defences of Donnarumma are racking up and what City are witnessing is fundamental problems from somebody described as the best the world has to offer.

Maresca has rejected the idea that summer signing Geronimo Rulli, a 34-year-old Argentina international, could take over the gloves, claiming that City line-ups are always ‘Gigio plus 10’. Rulli understood his lot when joining from Marseille, to feature in domestic cup competitions, and was happy with that.

Gianluigi Donnarumma had a night to forget in Leipzig this week, making at least three individual errors

But Man City boss Enzo Maresca will stand by his goalkeeper, claiming that City line-ups are always ‘Gigio plus 10’

Happy in a way that James Trafford was not, after making it clear that one season as Donnarumma’s understudy was not palatable.

He has flourished at Leeds United so far this season, leading to some observers criticising Hugo Viana for letting him go, only to blunder for a goal at Bournemouth last weekend. Worth remembering that it does happen to all of them at some point.

Trafford did not appear ready for the big time last year when starting the season ahead of the wantaway Ederson and City had their eyes on Donnarumma months before landing him – a £26million deal struck just as Ederson left for Fenerbahce.

Trafford will be ready soon and is pushing Jordan Pickford hard to be England's No1, but definitely wasn’t back then.

With Trafford gone and Maresca seemingly ruling out his No2 taking over – while also making a vague reference to taking stock over the international break – it appears that City would have no option but to stick with Donnarumma if they did actually want to bring about a change. January signings seem remote in the current climate of guilty verdicts and appeals.

But there is something outstanding that Donnarumma does offer, one that does set him apart. Maresca categorised the stunning one-handed save from Leipzig’s Christoph Baumgartner as one nobody else could make.

And while some hyperbole might be at play there, very few could lay claim to producing that kind of moment on a semi-regular basis.

Repelling Baumgartner is up there with Donnarumma’s instinctive save from Bryan Mbeumo at a crucial juncture on debut last year and thwarting Alexis Mac Allister in a victory at Anfield. The sort of awe-inspiring saves thousands pay money to witness.

Very few goalkeepers can claim to make wonder-saves as regularly as Donnarumma does

Donnarumma's impressive shot-stopping in the Premier League is evidenced by this graphic of every shot he has faced since joining City (red circles = goals, blank circles = saves)

Nobody across the Premier League has a higher save percentage than Donnarumma’s 71.5 since his arrival from PSG. More scientifically, only Bart Verbruggen and Senne Lammens have prevented more goals in that time – a metric measured by the xG of shots compared to how many goals were conceded.

Donnarumma has prevented seven goals (1.4 this season), with Brighton’s Verbruggen at 9.7 and Manchester United's Lammens at 8.1 across the same period. These are broadly encouraging numbers for City, despite Donnarumma's save percentage dipping to 69.7 this season – eighth among his peers, with Trafford way out in front on 79.5.

City will need to keep a careful eye on that downward trend from a 27-year-old who they brought to the club to act as the anchor, to bail them out in a way that Ederson struggled. That was the trade-off for his limited footwork, being incapable of playing through the opposition lines in a way the Brazilian could.

The wonder saves cancel all of that out. Donnarumma has been the goalkeeper’s goalkeeper for those alone. But were the certainty around that aspect of his game to waver on a longer-term basis, City should have decisions to make.

#1992. Coutinho 2.0? Liverpool make their move for Brazilian starlet after recent contract decision

Almost 14 years on from signing Philippe Coutinho, Liverpool are reportedly making moves to potentially sign another Brazilian playmaker who’s been attracting some high-profile European interest.

The Reds’ former number 10 spent five years at Anfield, during which time he scored 54 goals in 201 appearances and was a hugely influential figure on the pitch, frequently conjuring up moments of majesty.

He was sold in January 2018 and wasn’t around for the peak years of the Jurgen Klopp reign, although there’s an up-and-coming talent from Brazil who LFC will be hoping can become synonymous with a successful era under Andoni Iraola.

According to Sport Witness, Liverpool have made official enquiries with Palmeiras about 19-year-old attacking midfielder Erick Bele, with the Brazilian club prepared to start negotiations at €30m (£25m).

Paris Saint-Germain have also been in contact regarding the teenager, who signed a contract extension to 2031 with his current employers last week.

The youngster stood out during a recent training camp for Brazil under-20s in which he provided three assists across wins over Denmark, United States and Mexico.

Bele has an impressive record at youth level for Palmeiras, with 20 goals in 45 games for their under-20 side, although his development is being managed carefully as he’s made just seven senior appearances so far (Transfermarkt).

He plays mostly as a number 10 but can also be deployed on the right flank, similar to Harvey Elliott, and it attests to how highly his club value him that they’ve rewarded him with such a lengthy new contract.

An analysis from Future Ballers cites finishing, pace, dribbling, technique, heading, off-the-ball movement and creativity among his strongest attributes, marking him out as a well-rounded young talent who also boasts plenty of physical strength.

Even if Liverpool were to sign Bele in 2027, realistically he wouldn’t be challenging for a first-team place straight away, given his inexperience at senior level and the presence of Florian Wirtz in the Reds’ XI.

A loan move or two to clubs in mainland Europe would likely be arranged in order to enhance his development, but we can certainly see why Anfield chiefs have enquired about an exciting prospect who, in time, could have strong echoes of Coutinho.

#1991. VAR a scourge on the Premier League as Forest denied by off-field meddling

Almost £3.5bn was splurged on transfers this summer in a league supposedly described as the best in the world, so why does VAR continue to prove so ineffective and divisive?

Seven years after its introduction, it remains a scourge on the Premier League and here at the City Ground was another exhibit of maddening off-field meddling.

Tottenham Hotspur avoided a third successive defeat after the crucial intervention of VAR prevented Neco Williams from securing Oliver Glasner his first win as Nottingham Forest’s head coach.

The big moment occurred in the 65th minute. Morgan Gibbs-White’s chip over Antonin Kinsky should have been dealt with by Sandro Tonali and Jan Paul van Hecke but both players got themselves in a muddle and Williams bundled the ball in from almost on the goal-line.

Replays appeared to show the ball went in off Williams’ knee and he was protecting his face with his hands to avoid a stray boot. The VAR review ruled that Williams had handled the ball, yet in this billion-pound industry there was not one camera angle which proved entirely conclusive.

On this occasion the VAR official was Peter Bankes, recommending to referee Craig Pawson that the goal be disallowed. Williams said: “It’s a goal. VAR is there when there is a clear and obvious error and for me that is not clear and obvious. I’ve seen the images and the replays and at not one moment did I think I handballed it because I never did. I headed it in between my arms. I’m at a loss at that one, it’s disappointing. If you’re going to pause it, it’s going to look like it hit my arm but it didn’t hit my arm.”

Glasner and the other Forest players were also incensed, and once again supporters are questioning how critical moments in matches are being decided by officials sitting at Stockley Park. “I think the VAR can’t intervene when he is guessing,” said Glasner. “I told the referee after the game that I felt the goal should have stood.

“The VAR should say to stay with the onfield decision because it is about strengthening the referee. If it’s not 100 per cent clear, stick to the onfield decision.  We had a briefing before the season that the threshold for VAR intervention this year should be very high which is why this is wrong.”

While Tottenham were perhaps fortunate to pick up their first point, they are still waiting to score their first Premier League goal of the season. They did not manage a shot on target.

The grand £350m rebuild is proving a slow-burner and it is only Mykhailo Mudryk who will have cause to remember such a dull affair. Signed on loan from Chelsea on deadline day, Mudryk made his first appearance since November 2024 after being suspended by the Football Association following a positive test for performance-enhancing meldonium.

The Ukrainian forward was introduced with 16 minutes left, with his manager Roberto De Zerbi determined to reinvigorate his career.

Tottenham are still waiting for lift-off but De Zerbi remains convinced that his team will eventually click, particularly in attacking areas.

One of their summer arrivals, Omar Marmoush, wasted their best chance in the 16th minute by drilling a shot wide of the post. De Zerbi said: “In the last third we have to improve. We have to maybe keep more calm when we are very close to doing something important.

“If we improve in the last third I think we can score many goals because we have the players with big qualities. We could have scored three or four goals.

Considering we were only all working together on Thursday for the first time, this is the right spirit and the right way to move on.” On Mudryk, De Zerbi said: “He’s working to reach the best physical condition and he needs time.”

After the disallowed Williams goal, Forest were feeling further aggrieved soon after when Rodrigo Bentancur appeared to pull back substitute Igor Jesus in the penalty area. These are two teams clearly in period of transition and patience will be required from both sets of supporters.

It’s full time at GTech Stadium: Brentford 1 Sunderland 1

Pierre Sage has his first win while Alvaro Arbeloa has lost his first three Premier League games and go to Anfield next Saturday. Frank de Boer vibes.

City needed Donnarumma to spare their blushes with several good saves.

Brighton 1 Leeds 1. Pascal Gross missed a late sitter and Leeds are still winless in Brighton’s ‘new’ stadium in 11 visits.

It remains 0-0 so Spurs are goalless in three, both sides remain winless.

Iliman Ndiaye took a knock and has come off after treatment. He has sat on the bench, though, rather than headed down the tunnel, which suggests it is not an injury.

Enzo Le Fee equalises from the penalty spot.

VAR does not intervene after Lewis-Potter was penalised for holding. Le Fee chipped a pen straight at the keeper there last season.

Ellis Simms with the latest, clocking Donnarumma flush in the face with his close-range effort.

And it’s a third goal from a  left-back, but this time it’s the substitute Ben Chilwell.

Enzo jeered by Coventry fans when taken off was predictable. Replaced by Ayyoub Bouaddi.

Jaidon Anthony bundled the ball in but had used his hands.

And Mykhailo Mudryk is on for his first appearance since November 2024.

Forest are feeling aggrieved over that disallowed goal. Replays appeared to show the ball went in off Williams’ knee and he was protecting his face with his hands to avoid a stray boot.

Big cheer for Phil Foden when he came on for Rayan Cherki. Cherki has been creative for City and this might be trying another mode of attack for Enzo Maresca or saving legs for the Champions League in midweek. They have two full days of rest before facing Porto on Tuesday.

That is a big chance for Coventry. Loum Tchaouna got room in the penalty area and it needed Gianluigi Donnarumma to save low to his right.

Luka Vuskovic heads in from an inswinging corner.

Controversy at the City Ground – and it’s again a result of Var.

Morgan Gibbs-White’s chip over Antonin Kinsky should have been dealt with by Sandro Tonali and Jan Paul van Hecke but both players got themselves in a muddle and Neco Williams bundled the ball in from almost on the goalline.

The goal did go to Var for a possible handball by Williams, and it was ruled that the Wales international did handle it. Did look very harsh.

Coventry are still in this game but City have their chances to put them away. Enzo was deemed offside when he set up a strike for Haaland. The UK’s most expensive player has got better during this game.

Looks like it will be ruled out for handball.

Vitaly Janelt breaks the deadlock after Brentford were battered in the first half.

Keith Andrews is a brave manager. Having been forced into a change after 17 minutes when his captain, Nathan Collisn was injured, he shook it up at half-time by replacing three of his biggest signings, Kayode, Sangaré and Ouattara for Hickey, Yarmoliuk and Anthony.

There might be a VAR check but Neco Williams is in like Flynn when Tonali makes a bad mistake.

Mohammed Kudus comes on for Sávio and Andy Robertson for Destiny Udogie.

Igor Jesus and Daniel Muñoz come on for Ola Aina and Dan Ndoye.

Tyrick Mitchell has scored his second. What do they say about London buses…

Mitchell rampaging up the left, shoots. It’s blocked by García who tries to clear by hitting it straight into Mitchell’s foot whence it ricochets past Bernd Leno.

It was the culmination of a long passage of huffing and puffing after Marmoush had scudded a free-kick straight into the Forest wall.

Forest are clinging on a bit at the moment with some pretty desperate defending.

It was put in by Jacob Strand Larsen, who came on for Eddie Nketiah at half-time but he was offside.

With Tottenham appearing so toothless in attack, you have to wonder whether Roberto De Zerbi ends the long wait for Mykhailo Mudryk.

It is over 600 days since Mudryk last played a competitive match.

There is also the option of Dominic Solanke on the bench too.

Tanaka was offside when he turned in Stach’s free-kick. Leeds squander opportunity to double their lead.

Because of the 4½ minute VAR check for the Ballard ‘goal’ and an injury to Nathan Collins that forced the Bees’ captain off.

These are clearly two teams in transition.

Tottenham have spent over £300m this summer and are still waiting for lift-off.

Forest are embarking on a new era under Oliver Glasner with a style of play that will take time to implement.

It’s been a messy game so far with both teams struggling to impose themselves.

The best chance fell to one of Tottenham’s new arrivals, Omar Marmoush, but he drilled a shot wide of the post.

Josh King scores one and makes one. César Palacios with the rebound after Gonzalo García’s effort was parried to him.

Oliver Glasner’s wife Bettina is making her first visit to the City Ground today.

Glasner said that he is hoping to celebrate dinner tonight with his first three points since taking charge.

In a ding-dong match, the left-back, Tyrick Mitchell, pounces to fire Palace level.

Lewis Dunk saves Brighton after Calvert-Lewin had rounded Verbruggen and tried to slide it in on the angle.

Erling Haaland at the back post with a thunderous header – his 300th goal in club football.

Kamada was offside by a gnat’s whisker. VAR is making this job ridiculous.

Both Calvert-Lewin and Tanaka should have finished but Bogle was there to make sure. Elvedi spun on to the ball in the right of the penalty area to stand up a left-foot cross to the back post. Calvert-Lewin leapt and powered a low header hat Rushworth scooped out. Tanaka, following up, sliced his shot from five yards across goal where Bogle blindsided a defender to tap it in.

Kamada equalises at the Cottage, played in by an excellent pass from Pino.

Coventry fans are in good voice – and jeering Enzo Fernandez when he gets the ball. The Argentina midfielder has been quiet so far.

Messy start here at the City Ground with both teams struggling for fluency.

Tottenham are still waiting for their first goal of the season with a drastically reshaped team.

Danso was deemed to be interfering with play in an offside position, blocking the goalkeeper’s view of Ballard’s strike.

Disasi gives the ball away to Charles who finds Bobb. His pass sets up King for a shot which is deflected past Henderson.

Kevin Danso was standing in front of Kelleher in an offside position.

Was a Sunderland player blocking the goalkeeper?

Dan Ballard opens the scoring at the GTech from a free-kick.

Cherki makes headway down the left and sends over a dipping, menacing cross towards Enzo who is pushed high as a No10 but Carl Rushworth plucks it out of the air.

It’s Enzo Fernández replacing Nico O’Reilly not Ayyoub Bouaddi.

Enzo Fernandez will start, it has been confirmed, with O’Reilly injured in the warm-up

Fernandez is lined up in the tunnel ready to come out.

England left-back, who was slated to play in midfield, hurt his back/hip in the warm-up.

Seems to have a problem with his lower back or hip. He has been ruled out of the match.

One pleasing thing about the signing of Melvin Bard by Leeds is the prospect of it reviving oft-heard Elland Road shouts from 1989-92 of ‘Giyit Mel’ and ‘G’won Mel’ in encouragement of the sainted Sterland, the Zico of Fullerton Park.

The big headline news from Tottenham is that Mykhailo Mudryk is on the bench.

Signed from Chelsea on deadline day on an initial loan, Mudryk was once branded as a future Ballon d’Or winner by Roberto De Zerbi after they worked together at Shakhtar.

Mudryk has not played a competitive match since November 2024 after being suspended by the Football Association following a positive test for performance-enhancing meldonium.

Enzo Fernández’s record deal to Manchester City was facilitated by English-founded agency Unique Sports Management, it can be revealed.

Fernández sealed a £125m move from Chelsea on deadline day, equalling the UK transfer record of Alexander Isak to Liverpool a year ago.

Football Association documents due to be published later in the season will show Unique to have played their part in the biggest transfer of the summer.

Fernández is represented by The Elegant Game, headed by ex-Argentina international Javier Pastore, although he is not registered with the FA for transfers in England.

Unique, which also represented Anthony Gordon for his move to Barcelona, were brought in to close the deal, which was agreed between clubs on deadline day afternoon.

The English-founded agency have Marc Guéhi, who moved to City in January, on their books and their summer deals included Gordon to Barca, Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea and Taylor Harwood-Bellis to Aston Villa. Troy Parrott, who scored the winner for Real Betis against Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid, is also in the Unique stable.

Will this be third time lucky for Tottenham Hotspur after their £300m+ summer reset?

In typical Tottenham fashion, their start to the Premier League season has not been straightforward with two defeats, five goals conceded and none scored so far.

The popular opinion is that it will eventually click, but Tottenham’s supporters are still scarred by those two successive 17th-placed finishes.

Forest have won their last four games against Spurs, so it will be an early sign of promise if Roberto De Zerbi can secure a positive result here.

Enzo Maresca believes streetwise Enzo Fernández will give Manchester City an extra winning edge – as he told his record £125 million signing to forget about the size of the fee.

City made the Argentina midfielder the joint most expensive purchase in Premier League history with their deadline day swoop from Chelsea.

Maresca has opted against naming Fernández among his captains’ leadership group, which features Ruben Dias, Erling Haaland, Marc Guéhi and Gianluigi Donnarumma.

But the Italian – who knows Fernández well from their time together at Stamford Bridge – is confident his fierce competitive instincts will bring an added dimension to his side.

“I don’t know if it’s streetwise but he knows how to win,” Maresca said, who is in line to hand Fernández his debut against Coventry on Saturday. “When you want to compete or win, it’s much more important to have players that already know how to do that than players who have never done it in the past.

“Enzo is not the only one. This squad has many players who know how to win titles and how to compete and this is what we are looking for.

“I know Enzo quite well and I know what he can bring to the team. He is a winner, [has] a winner’s mentality and knows how to win [after] the World Cup, Club World Cup [success].

“I just said he is a winner and when you belong to the squad and another winning player arrives, they are always happy.

“I can promise you that in the last four or five days, four or five players from the squad were asking if was coming or not because they wanted him to be with us. It’s very important that he is with us.”

Maresca said he planned to use Fernandez predominantly as a No 6 or No 8 depending on the game. “I see Enzo as a six, a little bit more deep, or [an eight] a little higher arriving in the box,” he said.

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of the Saturday afternoon 3pm kick-offs of which we are treated to a rare number this week as Sky and TNT Sports decide to inconvenience only 10 sets of matchgoing supporters rather than the usual 12 or 14. The matches start, purely alphabetically, with unbeaten Brentford hosting Sunderland, Leeds United travelling to Brighton and Hove Albion’s Amex Stadium where they have never won and have come away with only three points in their seven visits, the something’s-got-to-give quasi derby between winless Fulham and pointless Palace, leaders Man City hosting Coventry City for the Sky Blue Cup and Tottenham head to Nottingham Forest in pursuit of their first point to spoil the gaiety of a nation.

We have Mike McGrath reporting from the Etihad and John Percy at the City Ground and I will endeavour to keep you up to date with developments at the other three grounds via various methods. Forest vs Spurs seems the most consequential of the fixtures, not because either manager is in any danger but because now the window has closed it should give us a clearer picture of how Roberto De Zerbi plans to marshal his surfeit of wingers into a coherent attack that can break their goalscoring duck and how he proposes to organise a back four that have shipped five goals.

Fulham and Palace have come in for a lot of criticism regarding their recruitment and while I can understand the frustration of the former’s fans for doing so much business with Real Madrid, I think Gonzalo García is a proper player and will shine over the course of the season.

Palace, I think, are paying the price for the January splurge on Brennan Johnson and Jorgen Strand Larsen, not just the inflated fees but the sizeable wages on players who contributed almost nothing. I was at Leeds vs Brentford last week and there was plenty to admire about both sides but fear for Leeds’ so-far commendable resilience at their Amex knacker’s yard and wonder whether Sunderland will be able to live with Brentford’s pace. Manchester City vs Coventry, meanwhile, probably will not give us the Bouaddi-Fernández-Anderson £325m midfield from the start but we might be given a glimpse.
