#1970. Maitland-Niles’ last-gasp debut goal salvages Everton’s miserable week

At the final whistle, the first song the stadium DJ played was Spirit of the Blues and how those relieved Evertonians lapped it up after a week of angst.

Their team had been on the precipice of a defeat that would have exacerbated all the frustrations that bubbled away following the chaotic conclusion to the transfer window. Indeed, it was 10 seconds over the allotted five minutes of added time when the ball fell to Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

It had been three years since the former Arsenal full-back had played in the Premier League – his last goal in England was on October 30, 2019, in an EFL Cup tie with Liverpool at Anfield that ended 5-5 – and he would not have joined Everton if their attempt to sign Kenny Tete from Fulham had not failed.

But here he was 30 yards from goal, with no need to break his stride as Manchester United’s backtracking defenders presented him with an invitation to shoot. So that’s what he did. With one perfectly timed swish of his right foot, an unlikely hero transformed the mood of a club.

"That is something SPECIAL!"Ainsley Maitland-Niles earns a draw for Everton on his debut with an unbelievable 96th minute strike! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/HNdx9PxrUP

“Brilliant technique,” said David Moyes, Everton’s manager, who had only introduced Maitland-Niles in the 77th minute after James Garner had succumbed to cramp and could run no more. “We are still getting to know Ainsley but that was a brilliant goal.”

Only those with the coldest hearts would begrudge Everton this point, which was especially hard-earned given they had conceded an 88th-minute header to Benjamin Sesko. But there is no chance a disbelieving Michael Carrick will feel that way.

Benajmin Sesko puts Manchester United back in front! 👊 pic.twitter.com/MF3A9LyaY8

United should, really, have won this game comfortably. Everton were there to be exploited and when Bryan Mbuemo put them ahead early in the second half, they should have powered away into the distance. Everton’s effort was good but they were in danger of losing hope.

Yet, incredibly, United gave Everton two helping hands. They had not been in a position to assist last Tuesday evening, when phone calls from Merseyside to Old Trafford to take Joshua Zirkzee on loan were met with rejection. But the second half display more than made up for that.

“We’re bitterly disappointed,” said Carrick, who was one step removed from having steam puffing from his ears. “All the work that went into putting us in that position at different stages to then come away like that… it’s not a great feeling. It feels like a defeat. It’s a bit of a cliché to say.”

But clichés are true. First United were passive when Tyrique George crashed in a brilliant right-footed drive in the 83rd minute and then, after Sesko profited from Jordan Pickford’s weak hands, they were passive again in allowing Everton to build the move that ended up with Maitland-Niles’ howitzer.

How had it come to this? It was beautiful bedlam, the kind of joy that only football delivers, but for long periods it felt like it was an opportunity for United. There was anticipation that Everton’s fans would create a furnace but there was also the fear it would be dispiritingly quiet.

Had this fixture been at Goodison Park, with its steep stands, tight confines and acoustics that split your ears, United would have been aware of the siege mentality as soon as their bus rolled up outside the stadium but their new sparkling home is rather more hospitable.

This is no criticism of the home crowd – it is anything but. Why should it always fall to them to bail out the failings of those in charge when those in charge, specifically the executives and recruitment department, have given them scant reason to have hope?

The route to victory for United, then, was relatively straightforward: for all Everton’s initial huff and puff, it always appeared that it would be a case of the away team repeating the simple things, retaining their concentration and waiting for a breakthrough.

It could have come as early as the eighth minute. Luke Shaw’s deep cross to the back post picked out Mbuemo, whose cushioned header invited Bruno Fernandes to take aim but the Portuguese’s volley clipped the crossbar with Pickford stranded.

United dominated and Marcus Rashford was central to it all, a scampering presence down the left who gave Merlin Röhl, playing as an auxiliary right-back, all kinds of problems. The only thing missing from his opening 45 minutes was a goal.

When Mbuemo scored so early after the break, it felt as if this was going to be one puncture too many for Everton to withstand and the anticipation was United would get the job done. In all fairness to Moyes, however, he was not in the mood to accept excuses.

His substitutions were all positive, with Jack Grealish changing the mood and Hayden Hackney providing dynamism. But it was the former Middlesbrough man who drove forward to give George, whose loan move from Chelsea was made permanent in June, the opportunity to smash an 83rd-minute bullet past Senne Lammens.

"That was unanswerable!"What a way for Tyrique George to open his account for Everton! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/c0HPRjWUia

“I told the players there would be no excuses and the players all agreed,” Moyes said. “They have hugely bought into it. And, you know, sometimes when you have [fewer] players it means everybody has to be ready. Sometimes when you have a small squad you have to find a way of making it work.”

They did just that. Pickford should have saved the header from Sesko that looked as though it had given United the lift, but Everton, with their manager belligerent and their fans sensing all was not lost, had other ideas. The noise they generated as Maitland-Niles’s goal went in was unique to this stadium.

As Moyes celebrated, shaking his fists and revelling in the positive turn of events, Carrick put his hand across his face and shook his head repeatedly. All the while, Everton’s fans sang I guess that’s why they call it the Blues. United’s head coach certainly had them. Everton, simply, had relief.

2 - For just the second time in the last 50 years, Manchester United have conceded 2+ goals in each of their first three games of a league season, along with 2020-21.Leaky. pic.twitter.com/B2Dk6Ioxkq

It felt like a win. The crowd was with us, we fight to the end and that’s how you get that type of result.

It’s amazing. Everyone wants to start like that and fortunately I did. I put my foot through it and it ended up in the top corner which I’m happy about.

I came here to work hard. It’s a team full of hard workers and I fit right in. I’m going to show I can pull my weight and give as much as everyone else, if not a little bit more.

Even I have a lump in my throat to see him do that after his original move to Everton in August 2021 was stymied by a late change of heart by Mikel Arteta. Don’t normally approve of badge kissers but he has waited such a long time for that and must have thought his chance had gone.

Just time to kick off before the whistle goes. Probably a fair result and that goal from Maitland-Niles was good enough to win a game never mind save it.

Everton 2 Manchester United 2 (Maitland-Niles) Stunning strike! Mazraoui had tackled Dewsbury-Hall in the box after more good work between Grealish and Hackney down the left. But the tackle diverted the ball to Maitland-Niles 25 yards out. And he wrapped his instep around a shot on debut that bent into the top left corner. What a goal!

"That is something SPECIAL!"Ainsley Maitland-Niles earns a draw for Everton on his debut with an unbelievable 96th minute strike! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/HNdx9PxrUP

Grealish’s beguiling feet dazzle Mazraoui down the Everton left as he tricks him to reach the byline. He cuts back a pass to Barry who tees up Hackney for a shot that he wafts miles over the bar. Grealish gives him a look as if to say, “Really?”

George finds himself in a near identical spot from which he scored and tries again with a thumping shot that flies into the side-netting via Lammens’ finger tips. He was offside on this occasion, though.

Five minutes of added time for Everton to level again.

Everton 1 Manchester United 2 (Sesko) Sesko wins the ball in the middle and works it out to Bruno Fernandes running down the left. He stops, faces up Maitland-Niles and waits for Shaw to gallop past him before rolling it into the left-back’s stride. Shaw fizzes over a cross that parts Tarkowski’s luxuriant barnet and Sesko, lurking on his shoulder, buries it from eight yards.

Benajmin Sesko puts Manchester United back in front! 👊 pic.twitter.com/MF3A9LyaY8

As Dominic says, below, Manchester United have been asking for this. They have been toothless since Mbeumo’s goal and the only significant threat, Rashford, was taken off for a left-back.

Everton 1 Man Utd 1 (George) A rasping, rising shot that beats Lammens at his near post. He absolutely larruped it after good work by Hackney to put him in space down the right of the box.

"That was unanswerable!"What a way for Tyrique George to open his account for Everton! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/c0HPRjWUia

If you largely try and defend a 1-0 lead and don’t go for that second goal, there’s always the danger of that happening. Superb finish from George to equalise but it’s been so passive from United. Asking for trouble and they’ve got it. Big 7 minutes plus injury time for them now.

Free-kick on the left, parallel with the penalty spot. Hackney bends it in with his right and Branthwaite heads it on target but too close to Lammens who oddly elects to punch.

Mykolenko gives the ball back from the throw-in as Fernandes serves his minute on the sidelines.

Dalot is booked for pulling Grealish’s shirt when the left winger had spun him.

Maitland-Niles receives a warm reception. I had forgotten that he has five England caps.

Bruno Fernandes goes down after kicking Tarkowski’s studs when his foot was raised. The referee does not stop play but books Maguire for complaining when the ball eventually goes out.

Garner almost immediately goes down and starts stretching his calves.

Mykolenko hurls a long throw into the Man Utd box. Dewsbury-Hall meets it with a shot that he catches sweetly but hits a defender. The ball rebounds to Armstrong who scuffs his attempt wide .

George has switched to the right to accommodate Grealish. I wonder if there was ever a possibility of him returning to Villa? Would Unai Emery treasure him?

“He’s back!” the stadium announcer has proclaimed, as Jack Grealish has entered the fray. The move has provided an immediate bounce but let’s see what the former England man can do to change the pattern of the game. Everton believe they have got a £100m player. It’s time to show it.

Grealish’s first contribution sends Mykolenko away on an overlap and Martinez messes up his clearance from the cross, shanking it behind for a corner that they defend soundly.

Manchester United corner on the left after Tielemans’ 25-yard shot was deflected behind. Fernandes plays it along the ground to Shaw in the D. The left-back’s control spoons the ball up with his left so he improvises a right-foot volley with his swinger, dragging it predictably wide.

Rohl is beaten yet again by Rashford and works his way into the book after pulling him back. It’s been hard going for the Everton right back against Rashford but United just haven’t taken advantage of it enough.

Jack Grealish is stripped and ready to come on.

Rashford jinks at pace 35 yards up the inside-left channel, chopping to the left and barrelling between defenders. He takes it too wide to shoot so cutely backheels to Cunha who pulls back his left foot to shoot from six yards but Tarkowski slides his leg through his gait and pokes the ball away. The away fans shout for a penalty but Cunha has no complaints.

Barry diddles Martinez by feinting to the right and then darting left to open a rout to goal. He hammers a shot from about 16 yards that Shaw slides across to block, diverting it to Dewsbury-Hall whose follow-up effort is a tame daisycutter that Lammens easily gathers.

It threatened to be the case that a Manchester United goal would puncture the atmosphere completely and so it has proven. The likelihood here is the away team will score again in the next 10 minutes to completely kill the game. Everton have endured a miserable week and this flat performance is entirely in keeping with the narrative.

Johnson cuts in off the right to run on to Garner’s pass and shoots from 18 yards. Martinez makes himself as big as possible and the shot clips his calf, sending it up before it dips threateningly, whistling over the bar.

Mbeumo heads out Garner’s corner. Dewsbury-Hall crosses it back into the box and Tarkowski tries to head it across into the middle. Manchester United clear their lines.

Shaw slides in to block Dewsbury-Hall’s shot after the attacking midfielder had manipulated an opportunity with a quick interchange with Johnson.

Key for Manchester United, who have taken the lead in a match for the first time this season, not to let up on the tempo with which they started this half.

Everton respond with a menacing cross in from the left, from George, I think, that eludes Johnson as he arrives in the middle a second late.

Everton 0 Manchester United 1 (Mbeumo) United were probing patiently from the kick-off, Mainoo the hub until he helped the ball down the right and Mbeumo drove in from the right touchline, splitting George and Mykolenko until he reached the 18-yard line and wrapped his left instep around a shot that he arrowed into the bottom left corner.

A brilliant run and a fine finish from Bryan Mbeumo! 👏 pic.twitter.com/IM9kVcdPkh

We hadn’t seen that Mbeumo in the first half – so much better, driving inside at pace and with intent. Good decoy run from Fernandes. Top finish from Mbeumo.

Both managers will want to see a lot more urgency from their sides in the second half. Rashford has been United’s most threatening outlet and has the beating of Rohl but Mbeumo and Cunha were poor in those opening 45 minutes and both guilty of turning over the ball cheaply when United were breaking late in the first period. Barry should have hit the target with a header from Rohl’s cross. But it’s been a lacklustre game, low in quality so far.

A drab match that came to life in the last few minutes of the half, creating good a good chance for Thierno Barry and Jarrad Branthwaite thwarting Marcus Rashford and Bruno Fernandes. Everton look wide open on the right side of their defence and Brennan Johnson is starting to make headway against Luke Shaw.

Brilliant sliding tackle from Branthwaite when Rashford, piling down the inside-left channel in full flight. Just as he was about to pull the trigger, Branthwaite launched himself to knock it away and leapt back to his feet to block Fernandes’ stinging follow-up with the his head.

Mykolenko’s long throw from the left raises the Man Utd blood pressure as they try to scramble it clear. The ball pinballs around the six-yard box, comes off Dalot last and straight to Branthwaite who catches it straight and true but clips the shot at Lammens.

There will be three additional minutes. Barry and Johnson link up again to send the rangey striker down the right but again he hits his cross/shot straight at a defender at close quarters. He can’t work an angle but tries to go through a defender.

Rohl and Barry link up in more orthodox fashion with an excellent, dipping cross from the right-back. Barry peels off Maguire and thumps his header wide. That’s the best chance of the game.

Neat one-two between Johnson and Barry sends the latter into the box on the right but his shot/cross is fired straight at Shaw. The crowd shouts ‘Hand ball!’ but it wasn’t and the ref waves play on.

Everton have had no spark at all so far. George goes down when challenged by Mbeumo to give them a free-kick on the left, 35 yards from goal. Garner hits a floaty cross to the right of the box and Barry heads it wide.

It was Johnson who was under scrutiny for a ‘foul’ on Martinez’ but it was just a hand on the back.

Branthwaite is winded when he collides with Pickford in midair defending a back-post cross. Seems to be OK.

Fernandes whips over a cross and Armstrong beats Martínez to head it clear. VAR is looking at Martínez’s claim that he was fouled. Now it’s been cleared.

Yellow card for Johnson for sliding into Cunha’s stride and raising his right boot to leg him up right by the byline on the left, 12 inches outside the area.

Shaw trips Rohl in the Everton penalty area as they fought for the ball from Branthwaite’s block of Rashford’s superb cross from the left. The winger was looking for a near-post runner but Branthwaite read it perfectly, certainly better than Cunha, and telescoped out a leg to intercept.

Given the chaotic end to Everton’s transfer window, the atmosphere was going to go one of two ways: bearpit or flat as a pancake. As of now, it’s very much the latter situation, and not even a first sight of Jack Grealish has enabled the volume to be pumped up. Everton are finding it difficult and special attention will need to be paid to Harrison Armstrong, who has been harshly booked but must now walk a disciplinary tightrope. The young midfielder has played encouragingly once again and is desperate to impress.

Ripples of applause for Grealish who comes off the bench to warm up. Armstrong is urged to shoot when fed by Garner’s curling pass up the inside-right channel. But he dithers and then plays it out to Johnson whose cross is no good.

Best move of the game to date should have ended with Cunha hitting the target. The silkiest bit about it was how Rashford lulled Rohl into a false sense of security with his first touch then tapped the ball past him in the next movement just as Rohl was engaging. Very clever.

Now Shaw reaches the byline down the left and cuts it back for Fernandes. Branthwaite again to the rescue, diligently doing his job and closing down the Man Utd captain. Merlin Röhl is a talented player but he’s no right-back against the well-grooved Rashford and Shaw combo.

Dalot let the Rashford pass through his legs to Cunha, probably deliberately but he might have been better placed to apply the finish himself. Cunha had the time and space to do much better than he did, though.

Cunha blazes a side-foot shot from 18 yards over the bar. It was put on a plate by Rashford’s cut-back from the byline after the winger was sent down the flank by Mbeumo’s clever pass.

Manchester united again open up Everton through the middle when Mainoo slips a pass to Bruno Fernandes who puts his laces through a 25-yard shot that Branthwaite bravely throws himself at and deflects wide and out for a corner.

Tielemans’ eyes widen as space opens up between Armstrong and Garner but he scuffs his 22-yard shot which floats gently down Pickford’s throat.

Shaw cuts out Branthwaite’s long pass to Armstrong who was running down the inside-left channel. Manchester United do not clear their lines convincingly and Everton come back at them, probing away with George and Armstrong.

Dalot is let off a booking inexplicably for pulling George’s arm after being spun by Everton’s left-winger. The crowd is irate at that and seething even more when Armstrong is yellow-carded moments later for wrapping an arm around Fernandes’ neck to stop him running away.

Big shout for a home penalty when Barry goes down, face first in the six-yard box when closed down ny Martínez but it was more of a belly flop than a foul.

Slick attacking move from Manchester United, zipping a dozen passes around Everton and ending with Shaw being slid down the left by Rashford. The left-back crosses from the byline and Mbeumo cushions a header to Bruno Fernandes who flashes a sidewinder volley into the crossbar.

In the grand scheme of things, this might sound the most ridiculous complaint you have read but Manchester United’s kit - really? When they play away at Everton, their kit has always been – and always should be – red shirts, black shorts and black socks. It looks odd with two teams playing in white shorts. This may seem a random observation but there we go... there hasn’t been any action to discuss in the opening four minutes!

Maguire returns to the fray as Everton pass the ball through midfield to Johnson on the right. His cross, aiming for Barry, is cut out by Maguire and cleared to halfway. Back come Everton until Dewsbury-Hall is too rough with Mainoo as the Man Utd midfielder tackled him. Free-kick.

Lammens kicks the ball the full length of the field and Pickford picks it up. Mbeumo momentarily is at right-back with Dalot at centre-half.

Maguire is OK to continue but he will be off the field for the mandatory minute.

Maguire headed the back of Barry’s head and splattered his nose. He should be all right though he might need the cotton wool nostril bungs for a while, like Blackadder, the pencils and ‘wibble’.

Big cheers goes around the stadium when Harrison Armstrong’s name has read out. Everton would likely have sold him had there not been a backlash from fans opposing his sale.

Concern here for Harry Maguire. Looks in distress on the ground, laying very still. Concerned players around.

Leny Yoro is warming up on the touchline.

Looks like he caught the back of Barry’s head as he went to challenge. Sat up nose receiving treatment on a very bloodied nose.

Everton kick off, attacking from right to left. The fans, as usual, are making a racket. Everton work the ball back to Pickford who clips a diagonal up the left. Everton play it towards Barry who collides with Maguire who takes a blow to the head.

The teams emerge from the tunnel, both teams in their home kits with the only twist Manchester United’s switch to white socks.

We’re looking forward to seeing what [Brennan Johnson] does. We know he is very capable [and shown it] in recent seasons. Let’s hope he can bring us goals and assists as he did for Tottenham.

We’ve needed them [the two deadline day signings]. Maitland-Niles is physically fine. I don’t think Jack should be yet. We’ve needed it.

That’s all gone now [deadline day]. It’s all about the football. That’s what people are coming to see and we’ll have to play as well as we have done in our opening two games, get a positive result. Hopefully we can continue to build on it.

Nothing different [expected from the fans today]. They’re always really good for us.

No surprise United remain unchanged from the 5-2 win over Ipswich although Carrick will be looking for his side to score first here and make life a little easier for themselves after going behind to Hull and Ipswich in their opening two games. Brennan Johnson comes in for the departed Iliman Ndiaye, who joined Manchester City for £65m on deadline day. Jack Grealish is on the bench for Everton.

Moyes issued a call to arms to Everton fans in his programme notes after a dismal transfer window that has left him with just 18 outfield players. The Everton manager warning there may be difficult times to come.

“Finally, I must stress the importance of us all pulling together,” Moyes wrote.

“We need to be strong again and there may be occasions when we may have to find a way to get through some difficult moments.

“It is something you have all done in recent seasons. Everyone has pulled together for the good of the football club and we may need to do so again.”

We did a lot of good things [against Ipswich]. No two games are ever the same. We have different challenges today. We have to be ready for that with some slightly different ideas. But the boys did well last week, trained well this week and we’re really looking forward to it.

The next result is always the most important one regardless of what’s happened. Building momentum, building a run, of course it’s important. It’s game-by-game, as you know, but this is as tough as it comes for us, Everton away.

It’s not a major deal, we’ve got the squad and we can cope with it [increase in numbers of fixtures with the return to European football].

Everton  Pickford; Röhl, Tarkowski, Branthwaite, Mykolenko; Armstrong, Garner; Johnson, Dewsbury-Hall, George; Barry. Substitutes Travers, Maitland-Niles, Keane, Grealish, O’Brien, Dibling, Alcaraz, Hackney, Graham.

Man Utd  Lammens; Dalot, Maguire, Martínez, Shaw; Tielemans, Mainoo; Mbeumo, Fernandes, Rashford; Cunha. Substitutes Darlow, Mazraoui, Mount, Zirkzee, Dorgu, Yoro, Santos, Heaven, Sesko.

"Whatever's gone on over the last few days is nothing to do with us as players" James Tarkowski is hoping Everton can get three points against Manchester United 🔵Watch Super Sunday live: https://t.co/0AejI4B8dF pic.twitter.com/PMWBO5Oiah

🔴 The Reds are unchanged from last week's win over Ipswich 👊

Mason Mount is fit enough for the bench and takes Shea Lacey’s seat

Brennan Johnson comes in for Iliman Ndiaye, now at Man City. Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Jack Grealish start on the bench.

Today's Toffees to face @ManUtd. COYB! 🔵#EVEMUN pic.twitter.com/8s2UrcwR59

Advertisement | GambleAware | 18+ Betting on the football tonight? Take a look at these tips and offers chosen by Telegraph Media Group

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of Everton vs Manchester United from Hill Dickinson Stadium. The hosts have made a creditable start on the field but four points from their opening two games cannot gloss over the discontent fostered by the owners and executives because of the credibility gap between their talk about recruitment and their paltry achievements.

The fact that their comeback against Bournemouth to earn a draw last week was achieved with Beto, Tim Iroegbunum and Iliman Ndiaye on the field and all three have now been sold with only Jack Grealish returning on loan to compensate tells its own story.

Speak to supporters and it is emblematic of ownership, they fear, who are prioritising Roma and view the Hill Dickinson as a terrific multisport and concert venue with a heritage football club attached. The bullishness of Angus Kinnear, the chief executive, rings hollower with each pronouncement and it is little wonder that the fans are so disenchanted.

David Moyes will not walk away but once again he has been sent into the fray against teams with £250m midfields armed with a spud gun. Having said that, we should not underestimate his capacity to rally the old “dogs of war” spirit even if the crowd is still yearning more for a “school of science” revival.

Manchester United won on their first visit to the Hill Dickinson last season when Benjamin Sesko came off the bench to score the only goal of the game and give Michael Carrick a fifth win in six league games as caretaker manager. They were far more fluid in their forward play during the victory over Ipswich last week but it was against an error-stricken defence and they continued to be as worryingly open at the back as they had been against Hull City in the opening round of fixtures with Luke Shaw and Lisandro Martínez having brain fades.

Shaw is a doubt today, along with Mason Mount, while Amad Diallo, Matthijs de Ligt, Carlos Baleba and Manuel Ugarte have all been ruled out. Only Christian Norgaard is absent for Everton but so thin is their squad, they will cast covetous glances at Man Utd’s bench, not least at Joshua Zirkzee who was the subject of a very late rejected bid on deadline day.

#1969. Transfer insider outlines Liverpool’s stance on selling Frimpong amid reported Saudi interest

Liverpool could potentially be open to selling Jeremie Frimpong for the right price in 2027, according to one transfer insider.

The Dutchman joined the Reds from Bayer Leverkusen almost 18 months ago and scored on his debut in the Community Shield, but unfortunately his time at Anfield so far has been dogged by several injury absences.

The 25-year-old has been sidelined with a muscle problem he incurred in the victory at Brentford last month, when he was forced off just seven minutes after his introduction as a half-time substitute, whilst he’s also shipped criticism over the nature of some of his performances this term.

According to Pete O’Rourke for Football Insider, Liverpool could ‘consider’ selling Frimpong next year, and the right-back has reportedly been attracting transfer interest from Saudi Pro League outfit Al-Hilal.

The Merseysiders won’t sanction a January exit for the Netherlands international due to concerns over squad depth amid the ongoing long-term absence of Conor Bradley, but club and player could be open to a summer departure if a ‘big offer’ is tabled.

The transfer insider also claimed that Andoni Iraola doesn’t have the strength in depth that he’d like, with the Basque feeling that his squad is lighter than many of the Reds’ direct rivals.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

First things first, there’s no way that Liverpool are in a position to consider offloading Frimpong in January, even if Bradley manages to return by then.

The latter will take time to fully get up to speed after not playing for nearly a whole year, and his own injury history isn’t the most auspicious either.

Ronald Araujo is currently doing an excellent job at right-back, but it isn’t his natural position and it remains to be seen whether or not his loan move from Barcelona will be converted into a permanent transfer.

If that does happen and Bradley rediscovers the strong performance levels that he’d shown prior to his knee injury, maybe then Liverpool would have more scope to consider a substantial offer for Frimpong if he’s not getting much of a look-in under Iraola.

For now, though, the Dutchman is very much needed at Anfield, and hopefully he’ll become available for action once the November international break has concluded towards the end of next week.

#1967. Michael Carrick accepts he won't be given time to emulate Sir Alex Ferguson as Unai Emery confirms Aston Villa contract talks in blow to Man United: Premier League LIVE

Published: 06:57 EST, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 10:06 EST, 6 November 2026

It's the final Premier League gameweek before the international break, and managers up and down the country will be speaking to the press.

Daily Mail Sport will bring you all the key news here...

Mikel Arteta said Max Dowman is raring to impress with the England Under 21s after being called up for the first time.

The 16-year-old Arsenal attacker has been selected by head coach Lee Carsley for the November friendlies against Portugal and France, with Dowman having previously represented England up to Under 19 level.

Should he feature in one of the matches, the teenager would become the youngest player to represent England's Under 21s, surpassing the record set by Jude Bellingham.

Mikel Arteta said Max Dowman is raring to impress with the England Under 21s next week

Arteta said: 'It's great news, I think he's very excited about that and now he has another contribution to do with the national team.

'Unfortunately, he cannot play for us in the next few games, but he will have the chance to play with the national team, which is great.'

Michael Carrick believes it's possible to emulate Sir Alex Ferguson's success at Manchester United, but accepts he won't be given as much time to turn the club's fortunes around as his former boss.

On the 40th anniversary of Ferguson replacing Ron Atkinson in 1986 with United one place above the relegation zone, Carrick's team are in an identical position having equalled Atkinson's club record worst start of one win from the first nine games.

A rousing win over Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday has lifted the mood around Old Trafford and eased some of the pressure on Carrick ahead of Sunday's game at home to Aston Villa.

Ferguson survived a barren three-and-a-half years in charge before winning the FA Cup in 1990. It was the first over 38 trophies over more than quarter of a century, and Carrick was asked if it would be impossible to match that.

'Well, it's not impossible,' said Carrick. 'Anything's possible. You've got to build, you know. You've got to be realistic. You've got to put things in perspective as well. The recent history that we've had and where we want to get to, it's not going to happen in a blink of an eye. It's not going to happen overnight. Success does take time, and we don't like having to spend time. But it does take a period of time to build.'

Asked if he will be given the same amount of time as Ferguson after 10 months in charge, Carrick replied: 'The game's certainly changed, no doubt. It always does. It had evolved to the stage probably after Sir Matt (Busby) in the years after that, to then Sir Alex.

'It evolves all the time. That's how it is. It changes. We've got to deal with what's in front of us. I get the comparisons. I understand it. There are always different things to compare, but it's we've always got to live in the present as well.

Michael Carrick accepts he won't be given time to emulate Sir Alex Ferguson at Man United

'Definitely use past experiences to help us, but we're all desperate to win football matches and win them as quickly as you possibly can.'

It was suggested that the 3-2 comeback win over Roma could be Carrick's 'Mark Robins moment' in reference to the striker's FA Cup winner against Nottingham Forest that was said to have saved Ferguson from the sack.

'More comparisons, yeah,' smiled Carrick. 'You always find something to compare, don't you? It's up to us to take it forward, you know. It was a fantastic night.

'It was nice for the supporters to end like that and to have that feeling, one hundred per cent for sure.

'But nothing's achieved yet, and it's one moment really in time that we need to use to move forward. But we need more of it, for sure.'

On Ferguson's 40th anniversary at United and his relationship with the Scot these days, Carrick said: 'What has not been said already? It's something definitely worth celebrating as a football club. That it's 40 years this week since he came here, and the impact on the football club, moving forward for all the time that he was here and that he's left for others to carry forward is incredible.

'I'm probably closer to him now and speak more to him now than I did when I was playing. I think the relationships change over time and that's only natural. Ever since I came here, the impact he had on me as an individual was immense.

'Not necessarily directly as in talking all the time and advice all the time. Personally, it was more the influence that he had and the habits that you try and pick up from him, as did everyone around the football club over that period of time. Then you move on and evolve a little bit into a friendship, which is really nice.'

Carrick confirmed that new £70million signing Carlos Baleba will be out for a 'number of weeks' after injuring his right hamstring against Roma, and United will wait to see if Patrick Dorgu can be involved against Villa after returning to training following a hamstring strain of his own.

Unai Emery has confirmed he intends to sign a new long-term deal with Aston Villa – ending Manchester United's hopes of hiring him if they sack Michael Carrick.

The Villa boss' current contract expires in 2029 and ahead of Sunday's meeting with United, Emery intends to extend the arrangement after positive talks with co-owner Nassef Sawiris.

'We were speaking about how we can set our project stronger with a [new] deal, yes,' he said. 'Nassef is very ambitious, a hard worker and his commitment to the club is huge. It's easy for me to have meetings with him as normally we are on the same page.

'It's about increasing our budget each year, and our revenue. Improving players, selling players, buying young talented players. This is the process and vision we should keep for the future.

'I had a very good, positive meeting with Nassef. Let's talk next week, trying to get everything that we have spoken about together.'

United's admiration for Emery has created a storm. Villa threatened to sue Sky Sports pundit Jamie Carragher for telling fans to 'shut the f*** up'. Supporters had objected to Carragher arguing that Emery should join United to further his career, and Carragher apologised for his crude language.

Villa's announcement on Wednesday that Sawiris and Emery had held talks also felt like a warning shot towards United.

Unai Emery has confirmed he intends to sign a new long-term deal with Aston Villa

Emery has never won at Old Trafford as Villa boss and despite United's poor form he remains wary.

He said: 'It's Manchester United. We haven't won one match there in the four years I've been here.

'It's very difficult for us. It's a fantastic club. They performed very well last year to get into the Champions League.

'This year in the league they've not been consistent at the start but they should recover. We played Barcelona in the Champions League on Tuesday and this game is of the same level.'

Enzo Maresca has not felt the need to dissect Gianluigi Donnarumma's troubling form with Manchester City's No 1 amid a number of high-profile errors.

Donnarumma was flat-footed in being beaten at his near post during Wednesday's Champions League win at RB Leipzig, following mistakes against Paris Saint-Germain and Aston Villa.

City's manager does not see the value in raking over the issues with his goalkeeper and believes the Italian's confidence is still high.

'He's good, overall he's good,' Maresca said of Donnarumma's mood. 'He's quite relaxed, in terms of recognising that he has done some mistakes but has made some good saves.

'There are players that when they make mistakes you need conversation with them, and there are players that when they make some mistake you just need eye contact to understand that he recognises.

'With Gigio it's quite easy because every time he has made some mistake or something that was not correct, he recognises immediately. Sometimes you don't need to be so deep with some players.'

Meanwhile, Maresca insisted that Elliot Anderson has another level to reach after an encouraging start to his City career.

Enzo Maresca has not felt the need to dissect Gianluigi Donnarumma's troubling form

The £116million summer signing goes back to Nottingham Forest on Saturday, with Maresca claiming that Oliver Glasner's side are in a false position.

'Elliot can do many [more] things, but he knows that,' Maresca added. 'We had a conversation before the last Champions League game, a nice conversation on understanding the game and slowly he is getting better and better.

'Elliot in this moment is playing more as the holding midfielder, but in future he can also play a little bit more up front.'

Fulham head coach Alvaro Arbeloa has backed Josh King to make the most of his 'special moment' after being called up to the England squad for the first time.

The 19-year-old has been selected by Thomas Tuchel for the upcoming Nations League games, having continued to impress this season after being part of England's pre-World Cup camp.

'It is a special moment for him and also for us as a club and our supporters. I think Josh is the pride of our club and supporters,' Arbeloa said at a press conference ahead of Saturday's Premier League game against Newcastle.

'He came to this club when he was eight and now you look at how he is playing and performing, so we are really proud of him. It is a big step for him and I am so happy for him because he is a very humble kid. You can see every day he wants to improve, to work and become a better player.'

King will again be central to Fulham's gameplan when Arbeloa's side take on Newcastle looking to build some momentum following last weekend's battling 1-1 draw at Aston Villa.

'For me, he is a very talented player. He can receive between the lines where there is no space,' Arbeloa said. 'He can drive, he can run, he can dribble with the ball, so he has everything, and we are working with him about his finishing.

'Obviously he needs to improve there and it is the most difficult thing in football, scoring goals, but his mentality, his character, he is a very mature player. You can't forget that he is just 19 years old, so it is unbelievable how he is performing. I think he has everything to become one of the best players in the world.'

After losing their last home game 1-0 to strugglers Crystal Palace, Arbeloa is expecting a response back at Craven Cottage. 'We know how difficult it will be to beat Newcastle tomorrow, they are a very good team, but we are playing well,' said the Fulham boss, who will be without defender Timothy Castagne because of a knee issue.

By HARRY BAMFORTH, LIVE SPORTS COVERAGE REPORTER

I think eight hours of coverage for the England squad announcement is enough, don't you?

In all seriousness, it's been real. Enjoy your weekend and thank you for joining us today.

One player I haven't mentioned yet is Dan Burn.

He became one of Thomas Tuchel's favourite picks in the backline last year prior to the World Cup. Then, of course, he played a huge part in that famous win over Mexico in the round of 16.

But it seems the Newcastle man can't get a look in anymore, after being omitted from Tuchel's squad today following being left out in the last extended break.

#1956. Stephen Robinson will carry the can for Aberdeen's woeful run but when do Dave Cormack and Lutz Pfannenstiel start getting it in the neck?

Published: 10:58 EST, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 11:14 EST, 6 November 2026

Few places are quite as spicy as Pittodrie when the locals have swapped the rustle of sweetie papers for the scent of blood in the nostrils.

Derek McInnes has been there. As have Stephen Glass and Jim Goodwin and Jimmy Thelin and plenty of others.

Current manager Stephen Robinson has been having a heck of a time of late too. The injury list is getting bigger and bigger as the patience with him dries up and everything points to it reaching crisis point on Saturday evening if the Dons, toiling for numbers or not, can’t see off Hibernian at home.

A number of punters didn’t fancy the ex-St Mirren boss from the off. And let’s be frank, results haven’t been good enough since he came in the door in March.

The reality is that Hearts are now the third force in Scottish football after a few years of jousting with Aberdeen, but that doesn’t mean expectations don’t remain high at Pittodrie.

A top-four finish is vital there in the wake of last term’s bottom-half struggles and beating the likes of Hibs, a club in a mess of its own right now, can be taken as a fair yardstick of how likely that is to happen.

Aberdeen manager Stephen Robinson faces a must-win game against Hibernian this weekend

Robinson needs a win. Should he suffer a fifth loss in six outings, he’ll be running the gauntlet for sure.

That’s the name of the game, but there’s just a couple of things before they bring out the tar and feathers and plan the great procession down King Street.

Not so long ago, sporting director Lutz Pfannenstiel was sitting around the dugout with interim Peter Leven. He was a big presence. Had plenty to say. What’s he up to these days?

Same goes for chairman Dave Cormack. He has chucked a load of money into his first loves, for sure, but he is seven years in charge now and it’s not exactly easy to figure out where the club is going with no new stadium, little mention nowadays about the ties with Atlanta United, the club in danger of ending in the bottom six again and the summer suggesting there maybe isn’t quite the same moolah bouncing around to go on transfer fees.

If it all goes belly-up against Hibs and Robinson cops it over another season looking destined for the doldrums, fair enough. But shouldn’t Cormack and Pfannenstiel be getting it in the neck too?

#1955. Villa end goal drought to finally give Emery’s new era lift-off

Unai Emery is building Aston Villa 2.0 and this was a night when his new kids on the block produced clear signs of lift-off for the next chapter.

Emery always springs into life on European nights and his reconstructed team secured their first win and goals of the season to leave Villa’s 1,700 fans singing in the rain.

Ten summer signings have arrived during a summer of upheaval, which included plenty of high-profile departures after the club’s Europa League triumph in May.

Yet this was an evening that will have further energised Emery on his return to the Champions League.

Nicolas Jackson, Zion Suzuki and João Gomes embody this new Villa team and all stood out here in Bruges.

Record £65m signing Jackson’s fine individual goal proved to be the winner to settle a chaotic, absorbing contest with the Belgian Pro League champions.

Jackson adds a third for Aston Villa after Sommer comes rushing out of his box! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/HZ1x3BkfK0

Suzuki, the £30m replacement for Emiliano Martínez, has clear presence in goal and he is Villa’s version of former Manchester City goalkeeper Ederson with his wide array of passing.

Gomes was also industrious in midfield to recover from what was a nightmarish debut at Brighton, where he was sent off after 40 minutes.

Despite all the changes to this team, talismanic captain John McGinn remains essential to Villa. He became their all-time leading goalscorer in major European competitions with his 12th goal and led by example again, as he has done so many times.

McGinn strikes to put Villa ahead in Bruges! 💥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FJnuxSwYwo

There were also hints of a strong defensive partnership developing between Pau Torres and Victor Lindelof, following the sale of Ezri Konsa to Arsenal last month.

“Fantastic, fantastic,” purred Emery at one point in the second half from the technical area, and Villa’s season now appears up and running.

Emery said: “This was another step forward and I am so happy and thankful for this. The old players need to keep our standards high and show everyone this is the only way we can achieve the process and reach our targets.

“It’s very important to start the Champions League with three points and hopefully this will give us confidence for the league. We are improving and we must work hard – it is the only way.”

Although Emery has established a reputation as the Europa League king, winning that trophy five times, this competition has proved more difficult to master.

His best run was reaching the semi-finals in the 2021-22 season, when his Villarreal side lost to Liverpool.

It remains a tournament in which he is desperate to make an impression, with Villa returning to Champions League duty here for the first time since their thrilling encounter with Paris St-Germain in April 2025.

Only five of that starting XI from the second leg of the quarter-final remain and one of them, midfielder Amadou Onana, is out until next year after sustaining a serious knee injury at the World Cup with Belgium.

With European heavyweights Barcelona, PSG and Borussia Dortmund to come in the league phase, this always felt like a game Villa probably needed to win.

They had only managed one shot on target so far this season before arriving in this historic city, but scored three goals before half-time.

Their opener came against the run of play in the 11th minute, with McGinn casually finding the corner after a lung-bursting run from Torres. McGinn has overtaken former Villa striker Ollie Watkins at the top of the club’s continental goalscoring charts.

Brugge briefly wobbled but were level eight minutes later when Hugo Vetlesen swept home from 10 yards, capitalising on space in the penalty box.

Vetlesen draws Club Brugge level against Aston Villa! ⚡📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/4ZYwPcMHim

Villa were back in front less than 160 seconds later, with Gomes teeing up Emiliano Buendía for an easy finish. Gomes was released in the box by a clever backheel from Jackson.

Buendia restores Villa's lead just minutes after Club Brugge's equaliser, and Unai Emery is LOVING it! 🙌📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/h2WGkwkTI1

Two minutes before half-time Yann Sommer, Club Brugge’s new goalkeeper, then had a severe rush of blood to the head by racing from his goal to almost the halfway line in an attempt to intercept Torres’s long pass.

Jackson edged the ball past him and held off a defender to calmly slot into the empty net. He underlined in many moments why Emery has pursued him for so long, after the pair established a strong rapport at Villarreal.

Villa appeared relatively comfortable in the second half until Aaron Wan-Bissaka was judged to have handled a cross from Joaquin Seys, after referee Sandro Schärer was advised by VAR to review the incident on his TV monitor.

It was a simple decision and Nicolò Tresoldi put away the penalty to stir life back into the home supporters.

Club Brugge are back in it from the penalty spot after Wan-Bissaka's handball! 👀📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pEanRJvimu

Villa defended resolutely as time began to tick away with Suzuki providing authority in goal. The first Japanese goalkeeper to play in the Champions League also produced a number of routine saves in a nervy finish.

This was a promising night for a new Villa era.

Full-time scenes in Bruges as Aston Villa get their Champions League campaign off to a winning start! 👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nYwtiQ6Xs7

Villa are defending with six at the back as midfield and defence merge into one. There are seconds remaining as Suzuki punts the ball up field and there is the final whistle! Villa make a winning start to the 2026-27 Champions League.

Another cross from the right is met, this time, by Tresoldi, but his header has no bite and Suzuki gathers.

Torres heads another Siquet cross behind for a corner. Brugge load the box but none of their players are able to get a meaningful touch on the ball before Diakhon slips just as he looks to get a shot away from the left of the box.

Slightly less mature play from Gomes, though. He bundles Vermant over and earns a needless yellow card.

Really mature play by Hemmings. Looking to break away, he simply puts his body between man and ball, inviting the challenge and winning a foul.

Villa are working hard in their compact mid-block and Brugge are struggling to find a way through.

Leko sends on Vermant and Diakhon for Potts and Virgili.

Barkley is one lucky boy. Attempting to play out under pressure, the midfielder gives the ball straight to Virgili, who cannot sort out his feet before offloading to Tresoldi far too late. A big let-off for Villa.

Gomes goes close after driving through Brugge’s midfield. He really should, though, have played in a free McGinn at the back post. Moments later Bogarde fires another shot goalwards but Sommer gets to it.

Villa have wrestled control away from their opponents. McGinn’s teasing cross evades everyone and Alysson’s cross takes a deflection which goes behind for a corner which is not up to much.

Lee hauls down Hemmings which gives Villa the opportunity to slow the game down. McGinn flights a delivery in from the left but Brugge clear their lines.

The ball comes out to Alysson who jinks in from the right, tiptoeing through a crowd, desperate to get a shot away on his left foot, but Seys does well to track his man and smother the effort.

Vanakan and Velesen and replaced by Tsawa and Lemarechal.

Yet another dangerous Siquet cross rains in from the right and here it is taken off Tresoldi’s toes by the tip of Lindelof’s boot. The defender did brilliantly to clear his lines at full stretch.

Hemmings burst towards the by-line and his cross trickles across the face of goal. Alysson is waiting at the far post but Seys does well to shield the ball and win a free-kick.

Villa’s best chance at putting this game to bed will come on the counter. And here McGinn plays in Jackson whose one-vs-one effort is stopped by Sommer.

Virgili from the left, Siquet from the right. Threats are coming from both wings and Villa need to get their foot on the ball if they are to take the sting out of Brugge’s attack.

Instead they allow Vetlesen a yard of space and his long-range sighter stings the hands of Suzuki who turns behind for a corner.

Emery switches out Buendia, Kamara and Wan-Bissaka for Alysson, Barkley and Bogarde before the corner is taken, and Suzuki stops the eventual delivery on the line after the ball spun off the post!

Another Virgili cross threatens to carve Villa open but they just about clear their lines. Then it is Siquet who delivers, this time from the right, but his cross just evades Tresoldi and Mechele at the far post. The home fans are invested in this, they believe their side can grab an equaliser...

Villa have got their tails between their legs here. From a position of strength, they have allowed the momentum to swing in the hosts’ favour and it has been largely self-inflicted.

Maatsen has a chance to break free but cannot build a head of steam before he is stymied.

Club Brugge 2 Aston Villa 3 (Tresoldi pen) Suzuki dives to his right early and Tresoldi slides the ball into the opposite side of the net. Just the one goal in it now!

Brugge have averted their attention to their right hand side, Siquet and Forbs attacking in tandem. A dangerous cross from Forbs is met by Tresoldi but he cannot get the requisite contact on it. Seys collects the ball on the far side and fires a delivery into Wan-Bissaka and out for a corner. Replays show that it comes off the defenders hand ...and referee Scharer is sent to the screen. He wastes no time at the monitor and awards a spot kick!

Villa do appear pretty comfortable here, despite some frequent pressure from Club Brugge.

Pau Torres has been outstanding so far at the back for Unai Emery’s team.

This is also a night where Emery’s ‘new’ Villa are coming of age, with Nicolas Jackson, Zion Suzuki and Joao Gomes also impressive.

Virgili then darts in field from his starting perch on the left. Tresoldi backheels the ball back into his path but Virgili’s effort is snuffed out.

McGinn, sensing Virgili’s growing influence on the half, takes matters into his own hands and leaves one on the Spanish winger, Siquet’s free-kick from deep is aimed at Tresoldi but Suzuki is wise to it and sweeps up.

Brugge are just reminding Villa that they are still there. Virgili is at the heart of things again, combining with Vetlesen who works the ball out to Forbs whose cross is well held by Suzuki.

Villa then spring forward, Hemmings breaching the Brugge box, but Buendia’s eventual effort does not make it through a thicket of legs.

Brugge are building with a three-man backline, sending Siquet forward high and wide. They’ve had much of the ball in the opening stages of this half, which is probably part of Villa’s plan. Emery’s side have settled into an out-of-possession 4-4-2.

Vanakan is booked for simulation after going hitting the deck off a challenge from Gomes. There is a knowing smile on the Belgian midfielder’s face which suggests the referee’s convictions were correct.

We are back under way... Siquet replaces Sabbe at the interval.

Nicolas Jackson is off the mark for Aston Villa. He beat Yann Sommer to the ball, held off a defender and was left with the simplest of finishes to round off a fine first half for Villa. pic.twitter.com/gWx6kUTlOX

Unai Emery has the new kids on the block but this Aston Villa team are hangin’ tough.

This has been a pretty chaotic first-half on the return of the Champions League but Emery will be satisfied with what he has seen so far. It’s very much a case of step by step for his reshaped team, but they should see this game out now.

It’s been a shocking night for Club Brugge’s new goalkeeper Yann Sommer. He’s just had a serious rush of blood to the head and was punished by Nicolas Jackson, who had an easy task to score Villa’s third goal. Sommer has probably ended his team’s hopes of a result here.

Club Brugge 1 Aston Villa 3 (Jackson) A shocker from Brugge, but in particular Sommer. Jackson races on to a nothing punt over the top by Torres, and the situation appears under control with two defenders in the striker’s orbit, but Sommer comes steaming out and Jackson nudges the ball past him before sliding it home into a vacant net.

Jackson adds a third for Aston Villa after Sommer comes rushing out of his box! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/HZ1x3BkfK0

A sloppy Torres pass out from the back goes straight to Vetlesen who picks out Forbs first time. The winger unleashes an effort from range but Suzuki makes a smart stop.

There is a shout for a Villa handball as Virgili prods a cross on to Kamara’s body, but his arms are clearly by his side.

Villa are presented with a great opportunity to break but the pass in behind for Jackson to gallop on to does not have enough juice and the move breaks down. Jackson does have a sight at goal moments later, but he’s only able to poke the ball wide off a free-kick from the right.

A really sloppy piece bit of play from Vanakan who cedes possession to Jackson and he’s straight into Brugge’s backline. He releases the ball to McGinn but the midfielder’s looping cross is cleared. Brugge need to take better care with the detail on their passes.

Jackson escapes the clutches of his marker on the half-way line with a deft spin and he feeds McGinn whose shot is blocked. The ball is worked to Hemmings after Torres is afforded space once more and a block takes it behind for a corner. Villa go short but the routine comes to nothing.

Maatsen flashes a dangerous delivery across the face of goal but the ball bisects Jackson and Buendia precisely and Brugge are able to clear their lines.

Brugge have certainly not given up the ghost, still looking to work the ball out to Forbs and Virgili on the flanks. Sabbe overlaps down the right but his ball to Vetlesen is cut out and Villa attempt to spring a counter which is snuffed out by Mechele.

Villa midfielder Joao Gomes is having a productive evening as he aims to recover from that nightmare debut.

He was sent off after 40 minutes of his first Villa appearance in the excruciating 4-0 defeat at Brighton and Hove Albion.

Unai Emery is expecting big things from the Brazilian midfielder, who departed relegated Wolves for £38m in July.

Wan-Bissaka drives down the right as Villa look for a third, but his cross is overhit and goes off on the far side. The right intent, though.

Club Brugge 1 Aston Villa 2 (Buendia) Jackson holds up the ball expertly before slipping in Gomes. The midfielder bursts into the box, outwitting Vetlesen before cutting the ball back to an onrushing Buendia who clips the ball past Sommer with aplomb. A crazy couple of minutes!

Buendia restores Villa's lead just minutes after Club Brugge's equaliser, and Unai Emery is LOVING it! 🙌📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/h2WGkwkTI1

Club Brugge 1 Aston Villa 1 (Vetlesen) Brugge are getting a lot of joy down the flanks. This time it is Vetlesen who finds space down the right and he spears a cross into the box. The ball is worked out to the left where the dangerous Virgili sends the ball back into the area and there Vetlesen is to sweep home. The stadium erupts as the Belgian champions restore parity.

Vetlesen draws Club Brugge level against Aston Villa! ⚡📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/4ZYwPcMHim

The Jan Breydelstadion had been very noisy but that goal has completely changed the atmosphere.

It is now nervy in the stadium and the Brugge fans are already starting to boo some of their players.

Villa’s first goal of the season and no surprise it comes from their talisman John McGinn.

McGinn strikes to put Villa ahead in Bruges! 💥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FJnuxSwYwo

Close! Hemmings races on to a cutback but his effort trickles just wide of the post.

Goalkeeper Sommer is penalised for handling the ball outside of his box. He had gathered a corner and had stormed forward to set off an attack. He changes his mind mid-throw and attempts to re-catch the ball but ends up wandering outside of his allotted space. The resulting free-kick crashes straight into the wall.

Sommer with an accidental handball outside his area! 😳📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fBbqPEYyUJ

Club Brugge 0 Aston Villa 1 (McGinn) Brugge will be really disappointed with that. Torres is afforded the freedom of Flanders as he strides up from his own half to the edge of the hosts’ box. He offloads the ball to McGinn on the right of the area and the Scotsman steadies himself before curling the ball into the far post, beyond Sommer.

It is that duo again, Virgili and Seys. They have responded to Wan-Bissaka’s advanced position and are trying to pin him back. Virgili cuts in on to his right foot and forces a save from Suzuki to get the home fans going.

Aston Villa are still establishing their identity with a new team but it has already become clear how much they will rely on goalkeeper Zion Suzuki,

The £30m signing from Parma possesses a wide passing range and much of Villa’s build-up play starts with the Japan international.

He is Villa’s very own version of Manchester City’s former pass master Ederson.

Much has been made of Suzuki’s distribution and he has already teased a couple of lovely flighted balls up-field. Villa’s defenders are more than happy to lure Brugge’s first line of pressure forward but have not yet been able to find an incisive line-breaking pass.

Seyes and Virgili combine down the left in Brugge’s best attack so far, but Torres is able to head behind for a corner, which is not up to much.

Wan-Bissaka has taken up a very aggressive position down Villa’s right and he earns a free-kick in a promising position. McGinn spins in a delivery which is only partially cleared but Maatsen’s effort from the edge of the box is smothered.

Villa get their foot on the ball from the get-go, circulating the ball around the back, before Suzuki launches a long ball up to Wan-Bissaka. The ball is worked to McGinn who feeds Buendia on the edge of the box but his effort flies just wide.

There is a minute’s silence for those affected by the floods in Nepal which is impeccably observed.

The players then retreat to their halves and Jackson gets us going!

Brugge and Villa emerge from the tunnel to the Champions League anthem... Here is this season’s introductory VT to whet the appetite.

As the rain lashes down in Bruges, you get the sense that Villa will have to dig deep to get a result and breathe life into their season. Both teams thrive on attacking transitions and the surface-level moisture will encourage breakaway moves.

Aston Villa 2.0 is clearly a work in progress after so many high-profile exits and 10 new signings.

Unai Emery has warned that it will take time for his new team to click, but this is an opportunity to spark the season into life.

Behind the scenes, Villa are feeling very comfortable about so much upheaval and it is the presence of Emery in the technical area which provides them with so much optimism.

For a deeper dive into why patience will be needed, read more here.

Brugge have conceded just two goals in five league games this season, but their Pro League opponents have threatened against the Belgian champions’ right side, especially in attacking transitions. Kyriani Sabbe is the more adventurous of Brugge’s two full-backs and the space he vacates will be inviting to George Hemmings and Ian Maatsen.

Here are a couple of examples of Brugge’s vulnerability down their right:

Don-Angelo Konadu, Lommel’s centre-forward, drifts out to the left and takes on Lee Han-beom whose centre-back partner Brandon Mechele has committed too far forward. As such, the space between Lee and covering left-back Joaquin Seys is too big and Freddie Potts attempts to recover from midfield. Konadu earns himself a yard with a feint inside and his shot is well-saved by Yann Sommer.

In Brugge’s 2-1 defeat by Gent a week earlier, Leonardo Lopes punches in a pass into the left half-space for Monodu Sonko to latch on to and from there the inside forward draws a save from Sommer. Josué Vergara’s follow-up strikes the crossbar.

The Spaniard added a fifth Europa League title to his CV last season while also guiding Villa to a strong fourth-place finish in the Premier League. Emery was today announced as one of five nominees for France Football’s Men’s Coach of the Year award – one of the Ballon d’Or accolades.

Christos Tzolis enjoyed an outstanding season with Brugge in 2025-26, contributing 51 goal involvements in 52 matches. His haul earned him a £34m move to Arsenal, where he has continued in much the same vein, laying on three assists in four matches.

While Tzolis wears the No 17 at Arsenal, his former No 8 shirt at Brugge has been inherited by Englishman Freddie Potts, who made the move from West Ham to Belgium last month. Potts has made a strong start to the season, serving as Brugge’s midfield sentry and starting all five of the club’s matches thus far.

One player to keep an eye on for Club Brugge is midfielder Freddie Potts.

He was signed from West Ham last month for a significant fee and lifted the Europa Conference League trophy when David Moyes was in charge.

Also in the Brugge team is Carlos Forbs, the former Manchester City trainee who had a poor loan spell at Wolves a couple of seasons back.

One player who will have many memories of this stadium is Villa centre-back Tyrone Mings.

Who can forget that bewildering moment in November 2024 when Mings picked up the ball inside the penalty area?

Club Brugge are awarded a penalty after Tyrone Mings picks the ball up inside his own area 😳📺 @tntsports & @discoveryplusUK pic.twitter.com/wpAqjMW8pn

Everybody loves a redemption story and on his return a few months later he produced a brilliant individual performance which included an incredible goal-line clearance to save his team.

Mings is on the bench today. Matty Cash is out with a muscle issue so there is a first start for summer signing Aaron Wan-Bissaka.

Addressing the media in Monday’s pre-match press conference, Unai Emery was asked about the challenges of taking Aston Villa into another season in Europe with a significantly changed squad. He said: “To continue in this level, changing some players, key players, but those key players we changed this year as well before the last year we were changing – not like this year, because this year was more players than normal, but we are replacing them.

“We have the players with experience like here with Emiliano [Buendía] and they deserve to continue here trying take now more responsibility and try to give the players we have … Of course we have now new players with a lot of experience like Goretska for example, and we have some young players, they are coming from [big] clubs like Garnacho, Mbaye or Jackson. We must try to adapt them in our structure tactically and arrive [at that point] as fast as possible … We need time, I don’t know if we need time or not, it’s not for me something I’m thinking about, I am thinking about competing. To compete [in] each match.

“We started the Premier League, the first competition, as our objective at the end of the season, because through it we can achieve our objectives this year, and we’re progressing. Still not enough, because we are not getting good results. But [the match against Brugge] is a new test.”

The experienced Yann Sommer starts between the sticks, with in-form striker Nicolò Tresoldi leading the line. English midfielder Freddie Potts is one of Ivan Leko’s two pivots.

Our ground crew for tonight. 👥📃 pic.twitter.com/UB7FUi9ZDH

Emery makes three changes from the XI that started against Hull City. Wan-Bissaka comes in for Matty Cash who does not make the match-day squad. Joao Gomes is eligible to play despite being suspended in domestic competition while Pau Torres replaces Tyrone Mings.

How we start this evening to take on Club Brugge in the #UCL 👊 pic.twitter.com/d7ftzgnoIi

Aston Villa are back in the Champions League and in familiar territory with an unfamiliar team.

This will be their third match at the Jan BreydelStadion in less than two years but much has changed with the players that last competed here for Unai Emery.

Two of the goalscorers in the club’s last outing in Bruges were Leon Bailey and Marco Asensio, who are no longer at the club.

Of course, they are not the only players that have left and this is a new-look Emery team hoping for lift-off this season.

Villa are the Europa League winners but this could be a tricky evening against the Belgian Pro League champions.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of Aston Villa’s Champions League opener against Club Brugge. Unai Emery’s side voyage across the Channel to face the Belgian champions having triumphed in last season’s Europa League and finished fourth in the Premier League. The Villa mothership has since sailed into choppy waters, though, with a raft of big-name sales preceding a run of two defeats and a draw in the league. An opening-weekend thrashing by Brighton and Hove Albion proved quite the storm for Emery’s new-look crew.

Morgan Rogers alighted for Chelsea in a deal worth £117m, a record fee for an English player, and goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez followed soon after, while Youri Tielemans moved to Manchester United. Ezri Konsa and Ollie Watkins completed the exodus of leading men with late-August moves to Arsenal and Al-Hilal respectively. To remedy the outgoings, Villa twice broke their transfer record this summer, pipping Newcastle United to the signing of Johan Manzambi (£59.5m) before landing Nicolas Jackson (£65m, including add-ons), and added Taylor Harwood-Bellis and Ibrahim Mbaye on deadline day. Whether they can hit the ground running remains to be seen, but Emery has a task on his hands aligning his new recruits before the scrutiny intensifies.

Although Villa swept aside Brugge 6-1 across two legs in the Champions League quarter-finals two seasons ago, here Blauw-Zwart (Blue-Black) represent a stern test having made the Jan Breydel Stadium a fortress in last year’s tournament. Their only home defeat in the league phase came against Arsenal, with a 3-3 draw against Barcelona backed up by 4-1 and 3-0 victories over Monaco and Marseille respectively. Belgium’s second-most decorated club have won seven of the last 11 league titles and know how to win matches. In Yann Sommer, Ivan Leko has one of world football’s most experienced goalkeepers, who kept the most clean sheets in the 2024-25 edition of the Champions League (seven). Captain Hans Vanakan, Brandon Mechele and Joaquin Seys were part of Rudi Garcia’s Belgium World Cup squad, and German striker Nicolò Tresoldi already has four goals in six matches this term. English midfielder Freddie Potts could also feature, having settled in nicely in West Flanders having moved from West Ham United during the summer.

The earlier 5.45pm kick-off time, means Villa, Brugge, LASK and AEK Athens have the opportunity to top the 36-team league …at least for a couple of hours.

#1954. Derek McInnes will soon have a Rangers selection headache as two-striker approach assessed

Kris Boyd insists Ryan Naderi’s impressive form in front of goal has provided Derek McInnes with a selection headache he will be more than happy to have, with the striker stepping up in the absence of key attacking options.

The German forward has seized his opportunity in the starting line-up since club captain Lawrence Shankland and Youssef Chermiti were sidelined through injury, linking up effectively at the top end of the pitch with £9 million summer signing Kevin Kelsy.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The pair have struck up a potent partnership in recent weeks, playing a key part in five successive wins that have provided renewed optimism surrounding Rangers’ title credentials this season.

Former Ibrox marksman Boyd has been impressed by Naderi’s all-round game and development after starting the season well down the pecking order, although he suggests there is still room for improvement.

“There's no doubt Chermiti was going to be the one at the top end of the pitch and maybe Shankland behind him,” Boyd said. “Kelsey has come in and he and Naderi have struck up a partnership.

“Shankland will be back soon. He is different to the other two and I still think he’s the best finisher at the club. But he will have a fight on his hands getting back in the team. It’s a good problem for Rangers to have.

“At the start of the season they were creating opportunities but weren’t taking them. You do feel they can score goals, but, more importantly, this team has more of a McInnes DNA defensively. Back then they had to score two, three or four goals to win a game. Right now they can get by with a 1-0. You’d want to kill it off a lot quicker than they do, but it was another three points [on Saturday] and defensively very good.”

Boyd is an advocate of McInnes' decision to play with two strikers, having operated in that system throughout his own career. He believes the approach provides Rangers with a greater physical presence and gives the opposition more to think about.

“Overall, both of them [Kelsy and Naderi] bring so much to the team and the way Derek wants to play. He wants to get the ball forward and it's two big boys who will ask questions of defenders. Both of them have been scoring. If you wanted to ask for more it would be goals from the wider areas.

“I played that way all my career but football has changed. Derek has always wanted to have two strikers though. Even when they were struggling at Kilmarnock he’d go two up top with wingers. I do think if you are one of the best sides in the country, you can have two strikers on the pitch as long as everyone is doing their work.”

The title race remains finely balanced heading into the final international break of the year, with Celtic four points ahead despite Rangers having a game in hand.

Boyd believes McInnes will welcome the opportunity to take stock of his team’s progress, even if they have continued to find ways to collect points.

“I don’t think he will be upset about the timing of the break,” he said. “Football is about momentum but you do need that break or reset to remind the players about the run they’ve been on. You always feel the last international break to the one in the New Year is when the league starts to sort itself out. Derek will want them refreshed to kick on towards the festive period.”

#1953. 'Severe rowdy' behaviour fears over changes to York City's home ground

Proposals for the LNER Community Stadium include a self-service ‘Box Bar’ to cut queues, reducing its licensed hours, indoor sports matches broadcasts and outdoor events and performances.

An application from the stadium’s operator stated the Box Bar would improve customer service by increasing the points of sale for alcohol which would cut queues at peak times.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

But two objectors who have bought homes in the nearby Castra Park development said they feared the changes would threaten the peace and quiet of the family neighbourhood.

York Council environmental health officer Michael Golightly said the application should be refused on public nuisance grounds as the potential effects of the changes could not be measured.

It comes as Greenwich Leisure Ltd’s (GLL) application is set to go before councillors for a decision on Monday, November 16.

Changes proposed for the stadium, at Huntington’s Monks Cross Shopping Park, include allowing outdoor events including boxing and wrestling matches, live music and other performances.

Plans to host six events a year including three boxing and wrestling matches within the stadium bowl in May and June have been drawn up.

Those plans, lodged by the York Stadium Management Company, are being dealt with under a separate application.

The stadium’s licensed hours would also be reduced from the current 2am to 11.30pm daily.

Sales would still be permitted from 8am across all of the 8,500-capacity stadium’s licensed areas.

Non-sporting events such as showing televised matches on screens would also be permitted.

The venue would also be licensed to hold indoor sporting events and other performances, stage live music and play recorded music.

The stadium would be operational from 6am to midnight every day.

Plans stated the self-service Box Bar will be supervised by at least two members of staff to intervene if issues arise and prevent service to under 18s.

They added the stadium’s licensed areas would be monitored by CCTV at all times and other measures would be in place to manage licensed activities.

The measures, including plans to manage events where 500 or more people are set to attend, have been agreed by operator GLL and North Yorkshire Police.

But a resident who is set to move into Castra Park, which is on land between the stadium complex and Huntington’s New Lane, said they were extremely concerned.

The objector said: “Introducing a fast-service Box Bar designed to increase the speed and volume of alcohol sales, combined with broadcasting non-sporting televised events, will generate a severe public nuisance.

“The resulting noise, shouting, and rowdy crowd dispersal at 11:30pm will cut directly into the peace and quiet of a brand-new residential family neighbourhood.”

Another future Castra Park resident said the roughly 300 new homes at the development would be exposed to late-night noise if the plans go ahead.

They said: “Increasing alcohol availability and extending operational hours will draw larger, less predictable crowds into an area that now borders new residential streets and pedestrian routes.

“This raises legitimate concerns about antisocial behaviour, crowd management, and the safety of residents who will be living within metres of the stadium perimeter.”
