#1938. Sebastien Pocognoli notices major difference in key Scotland man Ben Gannon-Doak

Sebastien Pocognoli is delighted his prediction that Ben Gannon-Doak will enjoy a lot more action for Bournemouth the longer the season goes on has come true in recent weeks.

There were concerns following the last international window that the winger, who started two of Scotland’s four Nations League matches, would suffer from going back into cold storage on the south coast.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

However, Pocognoli expressed confidence that manager Marco Rose would utilise the winger more freely given the club’s European commitments.

Gannon-Doak has since featured seven times for Bournemouth, including four starts. He was even named man-of-the-match in the recent 3-0 Europa League win over AC Milan that shocked so many people across Europe. Many had doubted whether he could contribute sustained performances for Scotland while featuring so rarely for Bournemouth.

But Pocognoli, who is hoping to secure his first Hampden victory on Friday night against North Macedonia, is comforted that his forecast that Gannon-Doak would return to England and “smash it” has proved accurate.

“Ben’s intensity is totally different from when he arrived in the camp in La Manga (in September),” he said at Hampden on Tuesday. “You saw his press against AC Milan or in the other Europa League games, it’s totally different fitness now.

“I am very happy with him and I believe that if we are playing good football it doesn’t matter the shape, he’s in the best position. He’s a young lad, twenty-years-old, so he needs confidence and to feel the love.

“He’s a top player and top players want to improve every day. I like his mentality, it’s exciting to see it but what’s the most exciting is that he’s still to improve on many aspects of the game. If he can improve on being more clinical in front of goal he would probably have scored two goals in the last window.”

Pocognoli has noticed the player is happier taking on responsibility and is displaying more composure. He is thinking more about what to do next when he has the ball rather than absent mindedly throwing it into the box.

“His assist and crossing was more with the idea before ‘if I put a cross in Scott McTominay will make a bicycle kick!’” he said. “But you see a little bit more of him now thinking what the next action is when he’s dribbling. When he’s more efficient, I think he will be a different level. But he’s only 20 so it’s (already) quite exciting.”

Although it was a slightly underwhelming first international window for Pocognoli, the Belgian believes players such as Gannon-Doak reaped the benefits from the four games.

Scotland won once against North Macedonia, lost 3-0 to Switzerland and drew and lost against Slovenia.

“I said to the lads when they arrived in September there were a lot of players with a lack of minutes,” he recalled.

“I said that when European football arrives they’ll probably share it out more. I’m sure the last camp allowed a lot of players to go back to their clubs (with a bit of) bounce.

"If you compare it to the first camp, there are maybe only two or three players with us now who have been playing less minutes but the rest have continued (to play more). I think the camp helped them build the confidence and get some minutes.”

#1935. Chichester beat Bath in Oaklands Park’s tale of two cities

The visitors came into the match in fine form with seven wins and only one loss in their previous eight league games, whereas Chi’s form has been up and down.

City made just the one change to the starting XI who won at Frome.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Skipper Rob Hutchings again lined up at left-back with Isaac Bello on the other side, with Ben Pashley and Ryan Davidson in the heart of the defence. Max Evans started between the sticks with Joe Moore, Emmett Dunn, Lucas Pattenden and Worthing loanee Matt Burgess in midfield, behind top scorer Harry Bridle and Brandon Chebby.

The visitors were awarded a free kick in the third minute but Evans collected the resulting header. Then Chebby had a shot of sorts and Bridle turned the loose ball in to put City in front.

Donovan Wilson got Bath’s leveller 11 minutes in before Callum Wood’s corner was headed away by the Chi backline.

Pattenden nearly reached a through ball ahead of Bath keeper Harvey Richards after Evans denied Oliver Chamberlain and Pashley made a couple of blocks as Bath looked to go in front.

Nice play from Pedro Elawar allowed him to find room but Chamberlain knocked the ball out for a Chi goal kick. Emmett Dunn hit a weak shot at the mid-point of the first half before Borges beat a hesitant Chi skipper Hutchings – only to blast over the bar.

Star man Chebby fizzed over a cross although no one was there to capitalise, before Evans saved from Chamberlain.

Davidson received some lengthy physio treatment just after the half-hour mark and had to be replaced by new boy Will Sweet. It tranpired Davidson had suffered a broken jaw.

Hutchings got done down the right wing by Chamberlain, who pulled a decent save out of Evans.

When Sweet was man-handled by Parsons, and after a melee, referee Joel Lamping consulted his assistant and brandished a straight red.

The visitors changed it up at the break bringing on Reuben Reid, and Bridle had a shot blocked in the first minute of the second half.

The away team thought they had gone ahead moments later through Reid but it was chalked off for offside.

Dunn headed away a corner as the away side pressed once more and Bello’s shot-cross was simple for Richards before Burgess was impeded just outside the penalty area.

Wood delivered one across the danger zone for Bath but no-one was there. A disappointing cross was easy enough for Richards before Pattenden smashed in Chebby’s fine cross on the hour to make it 2-1.

The Chi No19 might have extended the lead following a Pattenden delivery in the 68th minute, and Enzio Boldewijn’s set piece went wide. Then Pattenden’s header was saved spectacularly by Bath keeper Harvey Richards before Bridle blazed one over the bar.

The Somerset side made a triple substitution on 77, and Pattenden tried to lob the Bath keeper but it was easy for him.

Chebby fired a left-footer off target before the ball was turned out for another City corner. Clarke came on for Dunn with five minutes to go and Munt replaced Bridle.

It looked like Richards had handled outside the penalty area as we entered six minutes of additional time. And Chi should have been 3-1 up but Moore somehow missed with practically the last kick.

#1932. Celtic's Europa League win over Besiktas a welcome boost ... but Mika Baur says belief has always been there

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 14:32 EST, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 14:41 EST, 6 November 2026

It's fair to say that the way in which Martin O’Neill got Celtic off the mark in the Europa League against Besiktas divided public opinion.

For many of those viewing a starting line-up including Jordan Lotomba, Seb Tounekti and James Forrest, the veteran lucked out.

The opposing take was that O’Neill executed a managerial masterclass. That the belated introductions of Callum Osmand, Camilo Duran and Colby Donovan constituted a textbook rope-a-dope approach.

Whatever the truth of the matter, and only O’Neill truly knows what it is, you could not possibly argue with the outcome.

Second best in the contest for an hour, Celtic improved markedly in the final 30 minutes and refused to accept a share of the spoils when it seemed destined to be their lot.

How you finish a match is, indeed, just as important as how you start it. And it helps, of course, when those who belatedly enter the fray bring not only goals but pace, panache and a positive attitude.

Midfielder Mika Baur has been a standout performer in an up-and-down season for Celtic

‘That’s what you want from the subs — to make an impact from the bench,’ said midfielder Mika Baur.

‘It says a lot for Camilo to accept the situation of starting on the bench. But to come on and make such an impact, producing in the big moments to score those two goals to win us the game was huge.

‘Ossie [Osmand] as well, he came on with a goal and assist. He won the ball as well and was working hard. I’m really glad for them.’

In every respect, Celtic needed a night like that. O’Neill walked off the team coach before the game knowing a loss would see him become the first manager in the club’s history to oversee five straight European defeats.

With the wider picture of just three wins in ten matches, the scatter gun had been trained on everyone at the club in recent days – the hierarchy, the players, the manager and his coaching staff.

‘The win was important after some tough weeks,’ Baur reflected. ‘But the belief and the way we work together as a team has always been good. There was never any problem with that because we always believed in ourselves.

‘We showed how we can leave our hearts on the field and put in a shift. It was important to get those three points and we deserved it.

‘Hopefully, we can go forward with the confidence from this game.’

Given the air of gloom which has hung over the club lately, the Turks’ opener, stemming from a ludicrous tackle by Lotomba, felt for all the world like an extension of so much which had gone before.

From the minute Osmand levelled with his first touch, however, the entire dynamic of the evening changed.

Celtic found something deep within themselves that just hadn’t been there up until that point. The positivity on the field was mirrored by the buoyant mood in the stands.

The introductions of Callum Osmand and Camilo Duran turned Thursday's clash on its head

‘The fans helped a lot. You could feel the energy,’ said Baur. ‘It was not just us players on the field who deserved the win — it was also everyone around the stadium and they brought the energy as well.

‘It’s an unbelievable feeling as a player to have everyone pushing you and being there for you. It gives you that last percentage of energy you need at the end.’

Technically impressive and tactically astute, Baur caught the eye on Thursday, just as he has done in most of his matches since moving to Glasgow from Paderborn for £4.5million in the summer.

Whatever criticisms can justifiably be made of the club’s recruitment across a number of years, the German has already justified the faith shown in him.

It’s easy to forget that he’s still only 22. The level of scrutiny he’s being subjected to in Glasgow is a new thing. So far, however, he’s shown up well.

‘Sometimes it works, sometimes it doesn’t,’ he shrugged. ‘But I hope people understand that as a young player it can be tough to be comfortable in a new country, a new culture and new club.

‘I have felt good in my first few months but it is a bit of a rollercoaster. Playing in this unbelievable stadium in front of these fans — you feel the pressure with some of the games we have lost, but I am getting used to it.’

Having earned his first full cap in September after being called up by new Germany boss Jurgen Klopp, Baur has dropped back down to the Under-21s in the coming fortnight but takes only positives from his experience of the last international camp.

‘I can understand,’ he said. ‘There are so many unbelievable players in the squad, especially in my position.

‘We’re talking about guys from Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund. I just do my best and hopefully they can see I am developing and improving.

‘I’m still with the Under-21s for the games against Belgium and Croatia, so that will be good.

‘European matches like Thursday can only help and I have to hope they see. I’m still young but I’ll keep doing my best and we’ll see what happens next time.’

#1931. Only one goal but three points for the Boars: Little Common 0 – 1 Roffey

Roffey made the long journey to Little Common determined to bounce back from the unlucky defeat against East Grinstead. Pat Gibbs was rested with a niggle after his first start back for months in the previous game, Hayden Skerry is still working back to fitness and the Pearse brothers still missing through injury.

Right from the start Roffey dominated possession and the hosts sat in a low block. Callum Kilkenny had the first attempt on goal when taking a return pass from Jordan Mase before shooting over the bar. Shortly after Kilkenny got round the back and Common keeper Matt Cruttwell had to block his effort with the rebound being scrambled clear. After nine minutes Roffey thought they had a penalty for a foul on Stan Berry but after consulting his assistant, the referee ruled it out.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Eighteen minutes in with nearly all the game in the Common half, Stan Berry, back from injury, cut in from the right and fired over. Chesworth showed a wonderful bit of skill but his cross to unmarked Kilkenny was just intercepted. Next, Jack Meeres came out of the defence to play a one two, but Cruttwell saved his shot. The home side forced a free kick which was headed clear with the return cross coming to nothing. Ten minutes before half time Tom Caplin and Kilkenny combined but the dangerous cross was blocked at the near post. A corner routine led to Charlie Gibson firing in a shot that brought an excellent save from Cruttwell. The ball was cleared long, but any hope of a break was snuffed out by Teddy Wood and Kilkenny.

Thirty-eight minutes and Harrison broke down the right and cut into the area, his cross shot bringing another good save from Cruttwell. Roffey’s pressure intensified as half time approached. Berry brought another fine save from Cruttwell and Mase’s follow up was blocked a couple of yards out. The deadlock was finally broken after a slick passing combination with Chesworth and Mase, released Harrison into the box and he slid the ball inside the far post. The Boars nearly doubled the lead a minute later, but Berry’s effort was scrambled off the line.

Five minutes into the second half a flowing move down the left ended with Berry driving the ball narrowly wide into the side netting. A minute later Kilkenny had Cruttwell diving low to his right to save again. Fifty-six minutes and Mase robbed a defender but shot straight at Cruttwell. On seventy minutes Mase hit a free kick narrowly over the bar as Roffey kept the game in the Common half. Entering the last quarter of the match. Mase hit a swerving drive that brought another great save from Cruttwell. Then the keeper made a more straightforward save from a Caplin effort.

Into the last ten minutes and despite the Boars’ dominance, the lead was still only one and Roffey continued to search for the second. Mase drove over the bar then took the ball off a defender and brought yet another excellent save from Cruttwell, this time low to his left. Wood tried his luck from twenty-five yards, but the home stopper was there again. The mist was now beginning to drift over the pitch as Bailey Moyo shot high and wide. As we entered the last couple of minutes it was still all Roffey, and Wood had his shot deflected into the side netting after a free kick with Jack Meeres’ header from the resulting corner being the last significant action of the match.

Roffey took the three points against a dogged Common side backed up by some outstanding goalkeeping. Despite only scoring one goal, it was a thoroughly professional performance with the home side being denied a shot on goal throughout the ninety minutes. The Boars move back up into the play off-places and now have a ten day break before their next match v Crawley Down Gatwick at the Fusion Aviation Stadium on November 17th. At present Horsham have no game that night so it would be great to see the Lardy Army and regular Horsham supporters there, with concessions for Horsham season ticket holders. The boars are certainly playing a very entertaining brand of football.

Roffey: Burton, Harrison, Gibson, Napper, Meeres, Caplin, Wood, Mase, Chesworth(Moyo), Berry(Hoarty), Kilkenny(Allen). Subs: Skerry, Mesquita.

#1930. Martin Keown explains what he 'can’t quite fathom' after Leeds United's win over Tottenham Hotspur

Arsenal legend Martin Keown has conceded he “can’t quite fathom” a decision made by VAR during Leeds United’s 1-0 win over Tottenham Hotspur.

Daniel Farke’s side claimed three points at the expense of Spurs on Saturday (November 7), edging past the North London club with a late Noah Okafor winner.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

It was not a game without controversy, as many felt Whites defender Jayden Bogle was fortunate not to see red for a challenge on Spurs winger Mathys Tel.

Keown is among those who felt Bogle was fortunate and has labelled the 26-year-old’s challenge as “reckless.”

He told talKSPORT: “It looks reckless. We’re just showing the clip, we’re not seeing it in real speed. I think he’s trying to somehow line him up to tackle him with his right foot. He plants his left and his left foot goes right down the Achilles of Tel.

“Actually, as he does it, he twists his ankle at the same time. It looks out of control. I’m pretty surprised, if we’re looking for consistency, I’m a little bit surprised he hasn’t gone for that. It does look poor.

“At least it should have been a yellow. It’s the studs, it’s the full six studs isn’t it? All the way down the back of the Achilles. I can’t quite fathom how VAR looks at that and doesn’t punish.”

Tottenham are complaining to Pro Ref about the decision and Keown’s surprise has been shared by former Premier League official Graham Barber.

He said: “I thought it was a very, very poor challenge, it was reckless at best but you could describe it as dangerous and endangering the safety of the opponent, and did it endanger the safety of the opponent? Well, the answer is probably yes, because he had to leave the field of play about five minutes later.”

#1929. Liverpool injury update: Virgil van Dijk, Ryan Gravenberch, Dominik Szoboszlai latest news and return dates

Liverpool will be battling some significant fitness issues during the international break.

The two-week pause in the campaign may have not come at an ideal time for Liverpool after bouncing back from successive defeats to Arsenal and Fenerbahce by beating Crystal Palace 3-1 at the weekend.

Nevertheless, it’s a chance for Andoni Iraola to take stock of where his team is at and build towards a huge game at home to a Manchester United side currently in the Premier League relegation zone.

The Spaniard has made it clear that his one wish from the final international break of the year is no fresh injuries - particularly after losing Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai during the autumn window.

However, Iraola may not get his wish upon news that captain Virgil van Dijk has withdrawn from the Netherlands squad, while Szoboszlai is awaiting results of an assessment after joining up with the Hungary squad.

With that in mind, here is the latest Liverpool injury news and return dates…

The Liverpool captain was called up by new Dutch head coach Xavi for the Nations League double-header against Greece and Germany.

However, it was confirmed on Monday that he - and Sunderland striker Brian Brobbey - had pulled out of the squad for fitness related reasons.

A statement reads: “Virgil van Dijk and Brian Brobbey have been dropped from the Dutch national team's upcoming international matches. Both players did not return fit from the past weekend's matches and are therefore unavailable.

“The squad thus currently consists of 23 players.”

Liverpool fans will be hopeful this decision is no more than a precaution, particularly after Van Dijk played 90 minutes in all four Nations League games during the autumn international window.

Potential return date: Sunday November 22, vs Manchester United (H)

Szoboszlai will be assessed to determine his fitness for international duty with Hungary.

The midfielder was forced off in the second half against Palace due to a knee complaint and Iraola admitted afterwards that the Reds No8 was not fully fit.

“Dom definitely wasn’t 100 per cent in the second half,” Iraola said. "Let’s see. The last thing we need now is to lose players in the international games.

"In the last international break we lost three very important players in Alex (Isak), Cody (Gakpo) and Dom. So now I'm praying - it's the last thing we need.”

Key Liverpool player at risk of Premier League suspension before Man Utd clash

Liverpool dealt new fitness scare ahead of Man Utd showdown

Liverpool star in surprise international call-up after injury lay-off

Potential return date: Sunday November 22, vs Manchester United (H)

Ryan Gravenberch has missed Liverpool’s last two games with a heel injury. There was hope the Dutchman would return for the trip to Selhurst Park, but was ultimately left out of the matchday squad.

“The only doubt we will have is Ryan,” Iraola said in the pre-Crystal Palace press conference. “The others will be the same as we have been.

“The Ryan Gravenberch thing is a day-to-day thing, it’s a matter of pain. Let’s see if he can deal with the pain and he can help us.”

With the injury severe enough to prevent the midfielder from being called up by Xavi for the Netherlands’ Nations League double-header, Gravenberch must be considered a major doubt to face Man United.

Potential return date: Sunday November 22, vs Manchester United (H)

Jeremie Frimpong picked up a muscle injury during the comeback win over Brentford last month, resulting in another lay-off for the full-back since his arrival from Bayer Leverkusen.

Like compatriots Van Dijk and Gravenberch, he will not be representing the Dutch during the international break and it’s believed his return is not too far away.

In the most recent update of Frimpong, Iraola said: “Jeremie Frimpong is obviously a new muscle injury and it happened, I think, in the second or third minute he was playing, difficult to predict and we will have to wait until he recovers.

“But it’s going to be difficult, I think, before the [November international] break. We will try but it’s going to be difficult to have him.”

Potential return date: Sunday November 22, vs Manchester United (H)

Giovanno Leoni signed for Liverpool from Parma last summer in a deal worth around £26million, but a serious knee injury means he has been limited to just one senior appearance so far.

The centre-back made his debut in the Carabao Cup against Southampton in September 2025, but he was stretchered off and it was later confirmed that he had suffered an anterior cruciate ligament tear.

He was expected to miss a full year of action, which has proved to be the case.

He had hoped to have made his comeback for the recent September international break, but that has since been delayed.

“It’s taking more time than we wanted,” Iraola said. “The planning was to train with the team in this past international break [but] probably it’s going to be in the next international break, so we’ve lost one month in the process.

“Giovanni’s injury, I wasn’t here but talking to the medical department, it was not just an ACL – it was a bad injury, a lot of things around the knee were involved apart from the ACL.”

Hugo Ekitike has not played since rupturing his Achilles against Paris Saint-Germain in April.

The Frenchman was forced to sit out the end of last season and the World Cup, where it was estimated that he would be out for nine months to a full year.

He was included in Iraola’s squad for the Champions League league phase - which came as a surprise to many - with the hope that he could potentially return for the final two games in January, against Inter Milan and Lens.

The striker is thought to be targeting a comeback before the turn of the year.

Conor Bradley is another long-term absentee for Liverpool, having suffered a serious knee injury at Arsenal back in January.

The Northern Ireland international suffered bone and ligament damage in that match, which has kept him out for almost a year.

Iraola’s latest comments were positive, indicating that Bradley will soon return to full training.

“[He is] doing very well,” Iraola said. “I think [he is] in a good place. Conor is not so far from training with the group – not like full training but doing some things with the group.

“I think Conor is not very far from starting doing things with us."

It looks as though he could rejoin team training during the November international break.

Potential return date: Wednesday, December 2 vs Sunderland (H)

#1928. Ian Hart: Champions League or a trophy for Brighton? - Why not both

At 62 I’ve been very lucky to have watched Brighton all over England, Wales and into Europe.

During various holidays I’ve also watched - on the TV - in the US, the Caribbean, Middle East. Last week it was the Far East and this week it was the Gold Coast, Australia at midnight. But why was Sunday’s victory so poignant for me?

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Not quite Saul on the Road to Damascus, but it’s another 90 minutes of realisation. It was perhaps prompted by sitting, as with Singapore last weekend, with ‘neutral’ football fans and hearing their opinions of ‘our’ football club.

It reiterates the almost seismic changes the club has undergone since that dramatic afternoon at Edgar Street in May 1997.

However somethings don’t change and I hope they never will, as the Albion’s annual commemoration of Remembrance Sunday was both poignant and fitting.

But then on to the action. The arrival of Brentford and the respective chairman’s shared backstory bubbling under in the background. Whilst not quite the M23 Derby perhaps, it’s a game we now look forward to that little bit extra.

Albion never let Brentford settle and by half time - courtesy of two goals and VAR actually doing it’s job - the Seagulls were effectively home and hosed.

So, if I had to don my mortar board and gown (Google required for some readers) and give a ‘quarter term’ report, what would it be?

Wow! Second in the table and the highest scorers in the top flight. One of the two defeats, Chelsea away, was arguably a game we should have won. And given Chelsea’s sporadic form since, if they played again this weekend, it certainty would be a different result.

Playing with flair and panache to reiterate a soundbite from previous columns, we all just have to enjoy the ride. One thing is for certain, we are in the EPL for at least another 12 months!

It’s just what will that 12 months bring. The much coveted trophy? Hopefully.

But in modern day football, what is the real gauge of success? We all want to see Dunky up on a podium lifting a pot, but what if this form continues for the remaining three-quarters of the campaign, and Albion get that all important Champions League spot?

Whether us old dyed in the wool fans like it or not, financially for the Albion that is far more lucrative than a trophy, bar the league title.

And again whilst trying not to get too carried away, there are also two huge factors coming at us over the hill. Champions League qualification, would almost certainly mean huge changes in the club’s wage structure.

If we don’t pay our squad the ‘going rate’, then rest assured somebody else in our league, and we all know the clubs, will. And naturally we would also have to recruit along with the financial implications that would bring.

Whoever you are, you can’t do the CL on the cheap! But again to reiterate, let’s not get carried away.

Many of us remember domestic football long before the advent of the ‘International Break’, but we go into this particular one in the highest league position we’ve ever been for a said break.

So let’s just enjoy every second of it, and cue dear old Doris Day… Que Sera, Sera…….only 28 games to go!

#1926. Mauricio Pochettino has already given Manchester United an answer ahead of new manager talks

Mauricio Pochettino has previously revealed the Premier League is the “ideal place” for him to work, amid links to becoming the next Manchester United manager.

The Argentine, who managed both Tottenham and Chelsea in the Premier League, has emerged as the new favourite to replace Michael Carrick - who is reportedly expected to be relieved of his duties as Man Utd head coach.

Following a 4-4 draw at home to Aston Villa, United are in the relegation zone and will remain there throughout the November international break.

According to reports, Man United are anticipating a managerial change before facing bitter rivals Liverpool at Anfield a week on Sunday and Pochettino is the new leading contender, ahead of Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann.

It is not the first time Pochettino has been linked with the Old Trafford post as it was almost a regular occurrence during his time at Tottenham.

But would he be open to a move now, should the vacancy become available in the near future? Judging by comments made in an interview with L’Equipe earlier in the year, Pochettino would be keen to manage in the Premier League again.

“I miss the football scene in England. I love the country, its culture, the football culture,” he said.

“For anyone with a competitive spirit who wants to measure themselves against others and test their limits, it's the ideal place. Here, you have to give your best constantly.”

While Pochettino misses English football, his commitments to the USMNT could prove a stumbling block if Man United do end up making an approach for the 54-year-old.

After guiding USA to a respectable round of 16 finish at the 2026 World Cup, Pochettino signed a new contract in August to stay on with the national team and his deal runs through until the 2030 World Cup.

#1924. Leeds United given injury update on Gabriel Gudmundsson by Sweden boss Graham Potter

Leeds United defender Gabriel Gudmundsson could train with Sweden this week - despite being forced out of action with a hamstring injury at the weekend.

The 27-year-old is a key cog in Daniel Farke’s Leeds machine but had to be withdrawn midway through the meeting with Tottenham Hotspur on Saturday (November 7).

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

He was replaced at left wing-back by Melvin Bard, who produced a strong performance to help the Whites clinch a 1-0 win.

International duty with Sweden now calls for Gudmundsson, who looks set to be back on the pitch this week.

Sweden boss Graham Potter told Fotbollskanalen: “He's okay. The X-ray went well, but we need to see him and go through a couple of days of recovery to make sure he's okay.

“He'll probably be on the field with the guys on Wednesday-Thursday. There's no problem.”

When asked if Gudmundsson could start against Bosnia & Herzegovina on Saturday (November 14), Potter replied: “Yes.”

Gudmundsson could come up against a familiar face, with his Leeds teammate Tarik Muharemović a key figure in the Bosnia ranks.

Sweden will be on their travels after hosting Bosnia, visiting Poland next Tuesday (November 17).

Leeds paid a reported £10m to prise Gudmundsson from French outfit Lille in the summer of 2025 and he has proven to be an incredibly shrewd addition.

His form has kept Bard on the fringes, although the former France youth international staked a claim for more regular action with his impressive outing against Spurs.

Bard said: “[The manager told me] to play like I did in training - to defend well, also to attack and just to enjoy myself.

“I think I made a good entrance. It was also important to get into the match well, because the team had played a good first half. And also, Gabi had played a good first half, I’m thinking of him too, because he got injured. I think I made a good entrance.”

#1923. Mauricio Pochettino contract clause explained as Manchester United 'learn price to appoint'

Manchester United have finally decided to sack Michael Carrick, with Mauricio Pochettino the frontrunner for the Old Trafford job.

Reports emerged on Monday evening that a decision has been made to dismiss the under-pressure boss with the club in the Premier League relegation zone.

As many of the squad fly out for international duty with their respective nations, work will now begin at the club’s Carrington training ground to hire a new manager.

And former Tottenham and Chelsea manager Pochettino is the favourite.

ESPN report that Pochettino is the favoured candidate among Man Utd chiefs, but he will not come cheap.

Pochettino has not been involved in club management since his decision to leave Chelsea, by mutual contest, two and a half years ago.

The Argentine had spent just one year in west London, and was soon after lured by the USA national team to guide them into their home World Cup where they were knocked out at the last-16 stage.

Pochettino was heavily linked with a return to Tottenham before the World Cup, and was widely expected to leave the USMNT setup after the tournament.

However, in August, Pochettino signed a new contract to guide the national team into the 2030 World Cup.

But, with Man Utd now set to come calling, Pochettino is ready to head back to the Premier League.

BBC Sport report that Pochettino is open to the Old Trafford job and Man Utd will have to cough up to appoint him.

According to The Athletic, there is a buyout clause in Pochettino’s contract worth $10million (£7.44m) which Man Utd can trigger to bring back him to England.

However, the buyout clause does not cover Pochettino’s coaching staff, many of who - such as assistant Jesus Perez - has been with him most the majority of his career.

Pochettino has already given Man Utd an answer ahead of manager talks

Given it is the international break, Pochettino is currently with his USMNT squad, at the team’s training center in North Carolina, ahead of two Concacaf Nations League quarter-final matches against Haiti on Saturday and next Tuesday.

Pochettino is currently scheduled to speak to reporters on Friday at his traditional pre-match press conference.

#1922. Thomas Tuchel admits his relationship with Jude Bellingham is 'up and down' - but on the mend - as he reveals he's apologised to Kobbie Mainoo who is struggling at 'off a cliff' Man United

Published: 14:00 EST, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 15:27 EST, 6 November 2026

Thomas Tuchel says his rocky relationship with Jude Bellingham is on the mend after revealing he called his brother Jobe in to the England squad after some cajoling from the Real Madrid star.

Tuchel and Bellingham Snr have not always seen eye to eye during the German's time as England boss.

But Tuchel said today he hopes those days are behind him after he called 21-year-old Borussia Dortmund midfielder Jobe into this squad for next week's Nations League games against Croatia and Spain.

'It was a bit of an up and down [relationship] of course but we are in a good place,' said Tuchel.

'I love to be his coach. He's a top player, a very influential player and I think it goes both ways. If Jude was not feeling comfortable he would not perform on that level.

'In the moment you see he's happy to come into camp, he's happy with the role he has, he's fully invested and now to have the chance to have both of them is just the next step.

Thomas Tuchel has admitted he has an up and down relationship with Jude Bellingham

'I hope we have finished with the down. You never know as a coach!'

With injury to Bournemouth's Alex Scott and Arsenal's Myles Lewis-Skelly suspended for Thursday's Croatia game at Wembley, Tuchel sprung a surprise by elevating Jobe Bellingham from the Under 21s to the senior squad.

'Yeah Jude and I have spoken about his brother because I was aware it was always his dream to play with Jobe for England,' explained Tuchel.

'Jude was always saying: "Watch him, watch him he's good, he can make it". 'I would say: "Yeah we are watching him".

'I think he actually watched training very early in my reign. He came over and watched his brother train. We chatted and said it would be nice if one day he was with him.

'He was very kind and very polite and I'm glad to have him in camp. Everyone will compare them and he has to live with this.

Now Tuchel says he 'loves' to be Bellingham's coach after his brilliant World Cup campaign

Jude had a hand in brother Jobe being called up to the England squad for the first time

'They look similar, even in their movements, but they are very different players. Jobe is more defensive. I think they are also different characters, at least that's what I heard.

'He couldn't stop smiling when I called to tell him the news. He has the same beautiful smile like Jude so it's nice to have him.'

Tuchel's squad for what he insists are two important games was once again full of messages and insights into this thinking.

There was no room for Cole Palmer and Kobbie Mainoo after both players withdrew from the October campo with injuries. There was also no call up once again for Manchester City's Phil Foden.

Asked about Palmer, fit and ready now and in decent form at Chelsea, Tuchel said: 'It's not personal and we will never assume that he is not desperate to come and play.

'But the competition is on. It's about the ones who walk the walk and come to camp.

'Someone more intelligent once said to me: 'You cannot not communicate. You cannot not send a message.'

'So yeah. A nomination is always a message, yes.'

Tuchel revealed that he almost picked Foden – who hasn't played for England since March – after an upturn in his form but had second thoughts when he saw him relegated back to the bench at the Etihad Stadium.

'He is close and he will always be close,' said Tuchel.

'There were glimpses of the Phil Foden that we would love to see. He had these two matches with four or five goal involvements and assists and being so clinical.

Cole Palmer continues to be left out by Tuchel - while Phil Foden was close to a recall

'I got excited and thought: "That's it, that's, he found his mojo, he is getting back there". Then he dropped again and played again from the bench.

'I'm in love with him as a player. What is not to love?

'If you see the boy train it's just the highest, highest quality.

'But we're talking about numbers in an England shirt which are not in proportion to his talent and to his potential.

'If we can align this and become a regular City starter and be decisive, I think he has to be always an option.

'It was very close and it's also close for Eberechi Eze to keep his place with us. He's not starting for Arsenal.

'But the advantage was maybe that Morgan Gibbs-White and Eberechi Eze come again into camp. The advantage was that they have been in camp last time.'

Thomas Tuchel has told how he apologised in front of the whole England squad to Kobbie Mainoo for not giving him a single minute during the summer's World Cup in America.

Mainoo cut a lost and frustrated figure during England's campaign after a succession of players were picked ahead of him in his central midfield position.

The Manchester United star has not made Tuchel's squad for the forthcoming Nations League games with Croatia and Spain after withdrawing from the last camp with injury.

Tuchel revealed: 'He was hugely disappointed from the World Cup, and deservedly so.

'I said it in front of the team, in front of the staff.

'I said: "Sorry that I didn't pick you, you did nothing wrong, that is on me".

'He was disappointed and I think it cost him a bit of confidence.

Tuchel has noted how Man United 'fell off a cliff' - causing issues for Kobbie Mainoo

'He was excellent in training and in the way he presented himself through the tournament.

'So he was never a problem, the way he carried himself.

'Then he pulled out of last camp. I was desperate to give him the minutes. Desperate to include him in this new start, in the Nations League.

'But he then missed an excellent camp and also entered a difficult, difficult spell for himself.

'He was injured then Man United fell off a cliff a little bit performance-wise. So this is why he suffers from that.'

#1921. Man City survive tunnel clash and Porto fury thanks to Haaland double

Erling Haaland revealed on the eve of this clash how he loves chopping firewood in his spare time – and his goals set alight Manchester City’s Champions League campaign on a fractious evening in Porto.

So much for the new group stage of the competition taking time to warm up. This clash was a hot-blooded, bitter contest that spilt over in the tunnel at half-time, with players getting separated and tempers rising.

And City were not easing themselves back into European action either, they went full throttle at the start of a tough set of group games. With Enzo Maresca, it looks like it will be all-out attack to get the best out of this team.

They can look nervous at the back, particularly with the ball at Gianluigi Donnarumma’s feet, but have attacking weapons to hurt any team in this elite competition. This was a performance that their rivals will take note of.

“It was a complete performance on and off the ball for 95 minutes,” was Maresca’s assessment.

City will certainly scare the traditional heavyweights with Haaland leading their attack and taking an axe to Porto’s defence like he does with logs in his back garden. It was his 58th and 59th goal in 59 games in the Champions League, with his latest an expertly directed header off a post and a calm side-footed finish.

NO MISTAKE from Erling Haaland this time 💪He's put Man City 1-0 up in Porto 🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/UpKOqQA49s

There is an argument that Pep Guardiola could have achieved more in the Champions League, given City’s dominance in domestic football. They have been knocked out by Real Madrid in the last three seasons but this is a new City, different personnel and even a new look.

They wore their black and yellow away kit, inspired by “Manchester’s iconic worker bee” according to Puma, and grafted their way to victory here. Non-stop running going forward, and scrapping with Porto, too.

The Portuguese champions were not happy with Marc Guéhi’s challenge on Gabri Veiga and claimed an elbow was used, with the row carrying on in the tunnel at half-time with security guards separating the players. Rúben Dias also appeared to nudge a Porto official on his way to the dressing room.

“I didn’t see anything but anyway, you can ask how many times you see me or my bench stand up? Zero, for 95 minutes. How many times do you see their bench? So...” Maresca added.

Only Dias and Haaland remain from the starting line-up from the Champions League triumph three years ago, so this is essentially a new team with a new manager.

Erling Haaland seals the deal in Porto 🤝🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/10xSTtZ8nw

Phil Foden, on as a sub in that game, started at Estádio do Dragão after his horse Wreck It Ronnie defeated Najidi Storm, which started the Goodwood race with 1-33 odds and is now the shortest-priced loser in British racing history. The rest of the team are new to City’s challenge.

That includes Ayyoub Bouaddi, 18, who was part of a £320m midfield refresh following the departure of Rodri, who was named among the Ballon d’Or nominees a few hours before kick-off to highlight the experience and class City have lost.

Bouaddi, who cost £81.4m from Lille, made a good start in his full debut. The Moroccan teenager is neat on the ball and gets around the pitch, with the next step being able to dominate games like his predecessor.

“In his last game he lost two balls and stayed calm and was back in our box,” Maresca said. “This shows how good he is because any player after two [poor] passes panics, but he is just 18. Erling, Rúben, Mateo [Kovacic], they can manage these kind of games better, but you don’t expect it from a guy of 18. I didn’t see him panic.”

By Bouaddi’s side in midfield was Enzo Fernández, who sought to drive forward into space when City counter-attacked. He was among the players who, along with Dias, were reminded of their Benfica history by the home fans.

Diogo Costa tends to be linked with a move to the Premier League every summer, but has been a one-club man for his career so far. But he showed why clubs are looking at him with his first-half saves to deny Haaland and Rayan Cherki.

Porto’s legendary goalkeeper, Helton, was in the press box at half-time and would have been impressed with the saves, although he was not in his seat when Haaland scored the first goal, which came 94 seconds after the restart.

City had worked the ball around the penalty area, with Antoine Semenyo drawing out Costa before laying off to Fernández. Haaland’s header from the cross had such precision that the goalkeeper did not dive as it angled in off a post.

Still, Porto had their chances with Alberto Costa heading wide from a corner and William Gomes charging down a Donnarumma kick – with City’s most nervous moments coming when they passed around their back line.

Man City are living dangerously here! 🫣Donnarumma nearly gifts Porto an equaliser 😬 pic.twitter.com/otIfZTHmdn

But Haaland sealed the win as the game ticked into stoppage time, finding the bottom corner from Rayan Aït-Nouri’s cutback.

“It was an amazing game against the champions of Portugal. We knew it would be a difficult fight, man against man, they are a top team,” Haaland said. “They play amazing football. All the pressure, we have to deliver on the big stage and that’s what we did. We controlled the whole first half, created chances.”

For Maresca, the victory was also a challenge against Porto’s aggression, with the Italian coach adding: “I was very pleased. We know in this kind of game when you come here it’s always difficult or tricky. The environment, the way they grew up, it’s normal, but I think we dealt with that very good.”

Top performance, Enzo 👊✨ pic.twitter.com/ds0f207tpS

Man City have now won seven of their last eight opening matchdays in the UEFA Champions League 🔵Starting strong 💪 pic.twitter.com/CIjsMj4Dig

“I think we could have scored more goals, especially in the first half. We overall deserved the win and happy with the performance. If you think you can come to a place like this and play and not concede any chances, that is not realistic and it is normal. I am quite lucky as I have a squad of good players. It is a special competition and all the games are very difficult. He [Ayyoub Bouaddi] never panicked and was very good. The performance from him was unbelievable. I am happy to reunite with Enzo [Fernandez], who was very good.”

36 - Erling Haaland scored his 36th UEFA Champions League goal for Manchester City, equalling Sergio Agüero as joint-most for the Citizens in the competition.Inevitability. pic.twitter.com/HHbNadybxh

“I am so happy with how my teammates have welcomed me into the club. They are not just great players but great human beings. The fans have been absolutely brilliant and this is a new step in my career. Erling [Haaland] is an animal, a beast. Every time I am on the pitch, I will look for him and look to assist him. He is an amazing human being and helped me settle in. I am happy Enzo [Maresca] did all he good to make the move happen. I am so grateful for everything he has done for me and my family.”

5️⃣9️⃣ appearances 5️⃣9️⃣ goals@Erling's #UCL record 🤯 pic.twitter.com/v6IvpwC9vm

“Amazing game against the champions of Portugal. We knew it was going to be a tough game, they play amazing football. We had to deliver on the biggest stage and we did. We controlled the whole of the first half. We created a lot of chances. They pushed us for a good 25 minutes in the second half but we pulled through. These are the games we have to win. We have had a great start to the season.

“He [Ayyoub Bouaddi] had a really good game and he has been amazing in training. I think we have a gem there. We have to learn and Enzo [Maresca] demands a lot from us. We demand a lot from each other. It was an unreal atmosphere so I hope Enzo is happy with that.”

The final whistle is blown and Manchester City begin their Champions League campaign with a 2-0 win in Porto. Erling Haaland’s double gives Enzo Maresca a victory in his first Champions League game in charge of Manchester City.

Enzo has two shots from range in quick succession, one from a free-kick. The free-kick goes just wide and the second is saved by D Costa.

It has been an ill-tempered game and tempers have boiled over again. Rosario and Haaland are involved in a tussle on the floor, which then leads to a mass melee. Haaland and Rosario are both booked for their part in starting that. Haaland is pleased that he got booked but I am not sure why. Both played their part in that melee.

Enzo Maresca’s side will head home with all three points. Ait-Nouri’s cross from the left side of the box picks out Haaland, who first-time shot from 10 yards out picks out the far corner. A clinical finish from Haaland and Manchester City will start their Champions League campaign with a win.

Erling Haaland seals the deal in Porto 🤝🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/10xSTtZ8nw

That is really poor refereeing. Porto are denied two clear fouls before Rosario is then punished for a foul on Enzo, which was a foul but so too were the previous two incidents. Francesco Farioli is then booked for his protestations but you can understand their frustration.

Ait-Nouri has the chance to warp up the three points with an effort from the edge of the box but his shot with his weaker right foot goes narrowly wide.

Nothing comes from the corner as Hwang’s delivery to the front post is dreadful.

Haaland has his fourth headed chance of the game but this one goes over the bar from Ndiaye’s cross. Haaland has scored one of those chances but spurned some good ones.

Down the other end, Fofana, only just on, wins Porto a corner and whips up the home fans.

A final change of the night for Porto sees Fofana replace Veiga. One last roll of the dice from Francisco Farioli.

Whilst Manchester City’s lead is only 1-0, Porto will believe an equaliser is there for them. However, the momentum they were building 10/15 minutes ago has seemingly been lost and the visitors have managed to wrestle back a bit more control.

That is a big chance missed by Pepe. Gimenez receives it down the left and pings a cross to the back post. The cross perfectly picks out Pepe, who fluffs his lines and completely mis-kicks.

Manchester City are making their final two substitutions of the night as Kovacic and Ait-Nouri come on for Bouaddi and Foden. Ait-Nouri looks like he is going to play left wing.

Two more changes for Porto as Silva and M Fernandes are replaced by Gimenez and Moura.

Porto are going to make their first two changes of the night as Hwang and former Norwich man Sainz come on. Varela and Gomes head off.

For the second time in the half, Donnarumma is lucky. To be fair to the Manchester City keeper, the pass back to him is poor but he is then fortunate. His attempted ball out to his left is intercepted by Gomes but it rolls behind for a goal kick. That ball could have rolled straight into the Manchester City net or fallen straight back at Gomes feet with an empty net ahead of him. Donnarumma was very lucky on Saturday against Coventry to avoid a calamitous moment and he is lucky to avoid another awful moment for the second time in quick succession.

Man City are living dangerously here! 🫣Donnarumma nearly gifts Porto an equaliser 😬 pic.twitter.com/otIfZTHmdn

Ndiaye receives it out on the left before driving inside. He gets his shot away from the edge of the box and tries to pick out the far corner but it is too close to D Costa and an easy save for the Porto keeper.

A fine pass from Rosario inside his own half cuts through Manchester City’s midfield sends Varela racing through the Manchester City half. He plays it out to his right to find Gomes, who cuts inside onto his left before trying to beat Donnarumma at his near post but the shot goes wide.

Enzo Maresca responds to a shift in momentum in this game making a double change. Anderson and Ndiaye come on for Cherki and Semenyo.

Porto have started to gain some momentum and they want a penalty. Bouaddi is perhaps a touch fortunate not to be penalised for a foul right on the edge of the box but it may have been just outside the penalty area. You can feel the game starting to turn in Porto’s favour.

Varela is inches away from an equaliser for Porto and plenty of the home fans thought the ball was in the net. Varela sends a curling effort towards goal from the edge of the box but it goes narrowly wide.

That was a glorious chance for Porto to equalise. A corner is sent in from the left to the back post, where Alberto heads it back across goal. However, none of his teammates, including Silva, could tap the ball into the net. Porto should probably be back on level terms.

Donnrumma is a very, very lucky man. Porto would have had a certain penalty as Donnarumma completely flattened Pepe but the latter was offside so it is no penalty. Donnarumma has been booked but avoids a penalty, which would have been a guarantee had Pepe been onside.

Just three minutes into the second half, Enzo Maresca has made a substitution. Gvardiol, on a yellow, is withdrawn and Khusanov is brought on.

Porto’s legendary goalkeeper, Helton, was embracing Daniel Sturridge in the press box and they weren’t in their seats when the goal went in. Lovely move from City and Haaland steered in his 58th goal in the competition.

Erling Haaland moves 7th in the ALL-TIME UCL top-scorers list 💪🇳🇴📊 pic.twitter.com/oIkrPxm0gT

Haaland wasted two headed opportunities in the first half but he does not spurn this chance. It is a first Manchester City assist for Enzo, who clips in a cross from the left side of the box. Haaland meets it and his header glances off the far post and goes in.

NO MISTAKE from Erling Haaland this time 💪He's put Man City 1-0 up in Porto 🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/UpKOqQA49s

Gabriel Clarke on Amazon Prime has reported that there was some trouble in the tunnel as the two sides went off for half-time. Both sets of security teams for the clubs were forced to step in.

We are back under way in Porto. Tempers were really starting to boil over as that first half wore on so will that continue into the second half?

The former Liverpool, Manchester City and Chelsea striker has described the incident involving Marc Guehi and Gabri Veiga as a “nasty collision” and “it does not look good at all”. I think Guehi is a lucky man to still be on the pitch as some VAR officials would surely have recommended a review for that foul. Porto boss Francesco Farioli felt Guehi led with his elbow and the home fans were not happy with that as well as a number of other decisions in that first half.

All the stats are massively in Manchester City’s favour but the important statistic, the scoreline, remains level.

The first half is brought to an end and tempers are flaring as the two sides head off, with the game level at 0-0 at the break. The Porto fans and players are not happy with the officiating and Enzo is also involved in some antics.

Gvardiol needs to be careful as he is not punished for delaying a restart when you consider he is already on a booking. The Porto fans want to see a second yellow but the referee says the ball was moving so Porto could not take the restart.

Three added minutes to conclude this first half.

Should Guehi be in trouble here? He appears in real time to win his header but when you watch the replays he led with his arm. He catches Veiga right in the face and Guehi could be in some strife. However, VAR is not going to take any further action and Guehi can count himself lucky. The medics are on to tend to Veiga and you do wonder why VAR has not recommended a review. The ridiculous thing about that was that Guehi was not punished with a yellow card or even a free-kick. That clearly shows the referee did not properly see it.

Porto fans quick to remind Ruben Dias and Enzo Fernandez of their Benfica history. They jeered the pair when they got on the ball. Enzo is getting it from all angles at the moment, with Coventry fans taunting him at the weekend. He can expect more of that in the Premier League after his part in England’s exit at the World Cup, which led to Argentina players holding up a flag saying the Falkland Islands were Argentina’s.

Tensions are boiling over. They have been threatening to do so between Gomes and Gvardiol for a little while and now they do. Gomes steals the ball off Gvardiol and attempts to counter but is pulled back by Gvardiol, who is rightly booked. Gomes is not happy with Gvardiol and they come to blows.

D Costa twice denies Manchester City in a matter of seconds. First he saves from Haaland, then gets to his feet to deny Cherki. Manchester City are knocking on the door and you do feel like a goal is coming for Enzo Maresca’s side.

No goals in Porto but Real Madrid have their second at home against Inter Milan through Fede Valverde.

Manchester City struggled to carve out any genuine chances in the opening quarter of an hour but there are creating more and more opportunities, the latest falling to Foden, whose shot from the right side of the box looking for the far corner is saved by D Costa.

It is not often you see Haaland miss two good chances with his head in quick succession but that is what has happened. Semenyo cuts inside on the left onto his right and curls in a cross into a good area. He picks out Haaland but the Norwegian’s header misses the target. He knows he should have done better as he shakes his head in frustration.

Porto’s front three have struggled to have much of an impact in the game, in particular Silva up top, who has been almost non-existent.

A great save from D Costa to deny Haaland. Foden’s cross just before the byline on the left side of the box picks out Haaland. The Norwegian has barely touched the ball tonight but comes close to opening the scoring. However, D Costa is on hand to deny him with a fine save. Should Haaland have given D Costa the chance to save it? Maybe not.

Diogo Costa CLAWS away Erling Haaland's header 🧤Man City come closest so far in Porto 👀 pic.twitter.com/KVnBHdbNlH

In probably the marquee match-up of the night, Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid are taking on Inter Milan at the Bernabeu. Real have just taken the lead through Kylian Mbappe.

Semenyo cuts inside from the left and gets a shot away from the edge of the box but it is straight at D Costa. That was Manchester City’s first shot of the night.

Veiga has a shot saved at the near post by Donnarumma but the offside flag goes up. Veiga and Pep exchange a neat one-two down Porto’s left before Veiga’s effort is saved but Pepe was offside in the build-up.

Manchester City are dominating possession and perhaps it was a ploy by Enzo Marecsa to take it slowly and hog the ball in order to take the early sting out of Porto. The visitors would have been expecting the hosts would want to start hot so maybe they were willing to be slow on the ball in order to quieten down the crowd early doors. They have not had a shot yet and not really threatened the Porto goal but the hosts have not offered much going forward.

The weather in Porto really is horrible, the type of weather you would expect in Manchester in mid-November than Porto in early September.

Porto have a strong defensive record thus far this season but undoubtedly they will be tested a lot more tonight than they are in Liga Portugal. You would also imagine they will have to be clinical in attack as they are unlikely to create as many chances as they do domestically.

With it hammering down, Porto boss Francesco Farioli has swapped his lovely suit that he was wearing pre-game for a tracksuit top and cap. At half-time, he will probably head back in drenched like all the players if he is active in his dugout.

We are under way at the Estádio do Dragão with the rain still teaming down in Porto. Manchester City’s Champions League campaign gets going.

It has been pouring down in Porto but that has not dampened the spirits of the home fans, who are in fine voice ahead of kick-off. The pyrotechnics have gone off and it is loud inside the Dragão. It has been a positive start for Unai Emery’s Aston Villa out in Belgium as they lead Club Brugge 3-1 at half-time.

Enzo Maresca takes charge of his first Champions League game in charge of Manchester City as they have travelled to Portugal to take on Porto at the Estadio do Dragao. These sides last met during the Champions League group stages during the 2020/21 season. Manchester City won 3-1 at home before the two sides drew 0-0 in this stadium.

Manchester City were busy late on in the transfer window, bringing in both Iliman Ndiaye and Enzo Fernandez as they spent nearly £200m on deadline day alone. They come into tonight’s game off the back of three straight Premier League victories to kick off the Maresca era. Maresca has limited Champions League experience as a manager, which came with Chelsea last season. Manchester City have won their opening game of a Champions League campaign in six of the last seven seasons but this will be the first time since 2015/16 that Manchester City embark on a Champions League campaign without Pep Guardiola at the helm.

“It is a hard place to come [Porto],” said Maresca. “They have started really well. In the last 14/15 games in Europe they lost just one, that shows a difficult place to come, but we will try our best and try to win the game. It is a very, very good team. They have different players, but in terms of the team it is very clear in the way they play. They are aggressive without the ball and on the ball, they have a clear style. But we will try our best and try to win the game. The ambition is the same; try to be ourselves and to win games and then we will see.”

Porto, managed by Francesco Farioli, have won every league game so far this season and already sit four points clear at the summit of Liga Portugal. Farioli takes charge of his first game as a manger in the Champions League and the club make their return to the elite European competition after two seasons away.

“We are going to face one of the big favourites to win the competition,” Farioli said. “It will be a game that will demand that we be at our best, and we know that whenever we step onto the Dragão pitch, something special can happen. I am happy to be in the Champions League for the first time at 37 years old. This will be my first game, but we approach every game with the same attention to detail and the same focus. It is easy for the players to be motivated tomorrow [tonight]. But the key will be our strategy and our ability to execute it, individually and collectively.”

Porto were in the Europa League last season, making it to the quarter-finals, where they were knocked out by Nottingham Forest 2-1 on aggregate. The omens would not appear to be on Porto’s side tonight; they have only won two of their last 16 games against English opposition in major European competition.

#1916. Portugal boss Jorge Jesus claims Cristiano Ronaldo did NOT tell him he was retiring from international duty after fallout with superstar: 'I found out the same time as you'

Published: 16:01 EST, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 16:09 EST, 6 November 2026

Portugal boss Jorge Jesus insists he does not 'feel guilty' about Cristiano Ronaldo's international retirement and had no idea it was coming.

Ronaldo's explosive row with Jesus that escalated after he was left on the bench for a Nations League game and climaxed with the 41-year-old publishing a long statement hammering his manager, left their relationship in tatters.

And on Thursday, weeks after the dispute, Ronaldo announced his retirement from Portugal duty, bringing a sad end to his career on the international stage.

Jesus has now spoken for the first time about it, saying at a press conference: 'I don't feel guilty about anything regarding his departure. I respect his decision and, as such, his history cannot be ignored.

'I will never do that. Because he will always be a symbol, and I have built a strong friendship with him over this year and a half. Sporting-wise, he has now made another decision, and I greatly respect his decision.'

When asked if he thought he was the reason for Ronaldo's retirement, the 72-year-old added: 'No... Maybe I rushed things, but not because of me. It was in his head that, with more or less call-ups, this was going to happen. It was always going to be during my tenure.

Jorge Jesus, pictured at a press conference on Friday, said he did not feel guilty about Cristiano Ronaldo's international retirement

'I didn't speak to Ronaldo because I was thinking about calling him up. From that moment on, I was going to have time to talk to him.'

And Jesus insisted he had no idea why Ronaldo chose now to quit, adding: 'You have to ask him... The absolute certainty I have is that Cris worked with me for a year. We were happy at the club where we were, we were champions. I respect his decision at this moment.

'He would always have been with me throughout all these years that we were going to work together. He was the one who would decide. I don't know why he made that decision. What I do know is that he knew his time was coming, he was the one who would choose. And he chose. Only he can answer that better than I can.'

Ronaldo scored a world record 146 goals in 234 games for Portugal and won the 2016 European Championship as well as two Nations League titles.

But he will not add to those achievements now – instead stepping away after 23 years playing for his country.

In his retirement statement, he admitted that he had at times 'failed' and revealed that his decision was difficult, but felt proud of his work and willing to hand over the number seven jersey.

His final minutes in a Portugal shirt came against Wales in September, when he played 67 minutes in a 1-0 Nations League win over Wales.

After being left on the bench for their subsequent match against Norway, Ronaldo had a row with manager Jesus and flew away from Portugal's camp via his private jet.

Ronaldo never reached a World Cup final and cried after Portugal were knocked out by Spain in the last 16 over the summer

Marking his retirement, he wrote: 'To the people of Portugal, the day has come to return the number 7 jersey of our national team. I never felt it was exclusively mine. But for 23 years, I had the privilege and the responsibility to wear it, to defend it, and to take it with me to stadiums all over the world.

'Today has come the moment to hand it over to the future. It was not an easy decision, because some decisions are not made just with the head, they are also made with the heart.

'I was always demanding of myself. I always wanted more, I always believed we could go further. And I gave everything I had for this jersey. There were perfect afternoons and nights, there were victories I will never forget.

'There were defeats that even today I find hard to remember. I also failed, I also suffered, there were also moments when I was not able to give the Portuguese people what they so desired. But I never gave up. And above all, I never stopped feeling proud to represent Portugal.

'Throughout these years, I learned very simple things. Goals pass, trophies stay in museums, records end up being broken. But there is something that time can never erase: the place we occupy in people's hearts.

'If I ever made you happy, if ever a goal of mine made you hug someone, forget a problem, or simply feel proud of our country, then it was all worth it. Because being Portuguese is also that. We suffer together, we get up together.

'If I got this far, it was because we were always hand in hand. And to the Portuguese, to all Portuguese people scattered around the world, I want to tell you one last thing. There is an image I will always carry with me: the moment the national anthem begins. I look around, I see my teammates, I see the stands, I see children, mothers, fathers, and grandfathers, I see Portuguese people who came from so far just to be there.

'And during those minutes, we stop being different. There are no clubs, there are no colors, there are no classes, there are no professions, there are no opinions. There is only one passion: Portugal.'

There will be questions over the way Ronaldo's international career has ended – to the public, it appears to be on rather bitter terms.

Ronaldo was livid after being left on the bench despite warming-up for Portugal's Nations League win over Norway on September 27 – the first time he has been an unused substitute during his 23-year international career.

The highlight of his Portugal career was lifting the 2016 European Championship, even if he got injured in the final

That led to him skipping three training sessions and abandoning the camp for Portugal's last two matches of the international break, fleeing to Spain via private jet.

He did not even watch their next match against Norway because he was soaring away on his plane with his family.

The former Manchester United star was vexed at how Jesus had handled his press conference after leaving him on the bench.

Ronaldo insisted that Jesus had broken a promise to apologise to the 'Portuguese people' and his team-mates for not bringing him on.

He claimed he had been guaranteed 30 minutes of football against Norway after the Portuguese FA persuaded him not to retire following the World Cup.

The five-time Ballon d'Or winner even offered to retire if that was what the coach and head of Portuguese FA wanted, only for them to reiterate their desire to have him.

But most hurtfully, Ronaldo released a stinging 1,996-word statement accusing Jesus of 'broken promises'. He said the manager had agreed to deliver an eight-point mea culpa taking responsibility for leaving him on the bench after a supposed pact to play him.

Jesus did concede it was a mistake to make him warm up but gave a different narrative of events, saying: 'The match in Norway was not part of the plan I drew up for him. However, I felt that he had managed to recover physically from the first match and I warned him that I might have to use him. Cristiano agreed.'

In the end, Ronaldo was fined £215 by the Portuguese FA and technically banned for a month – though that was backdated, making him free for their upcoming fixtures. But fans – and the man himself – will now have to embrace the next chapter as Portugal aim to move on without the most illustrious player in their history.

#1915. What happened last time Mauricio Pochettino interviewed for Man Utd job?

Mauricio Pochettino has long been of interest to Manchester United, having twice previously interviewed for the manager job.

Pochettino continues to enjoy a stellar reputation in the Premier League thanks to his work at Tottenham over five-and-a-half years, during which time he twice came close to winning the Premier League title and took Spurs to a Champions League final.

The Argentine's time with Southampton, previous to Spurs, was also eye-catching, while his one-season spell with Chelsea, which ended two years ago, showed signs of promise before his mutually agreed exit.

So it was Pochettino's success at Spurs which twice previously attracted interest internally at Manchester United.

And as Pochettino emerges as the favourite to become the new Man Utd manager, we look back on the previous times he has been sounded out for the job.

Man Utd reportedly came calling in late 2018, following the sacking of Jose Mourinho.

According to The Mirror, Pochettino - who at the time had Spurs in third place in the Premier League standings and was six months away from guiding them to the Champions League final - was a standout candidate and had the approval of Sir Alex Ferguson.

However, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer was eventually given the caretaker role and then the permanent gig, and remained in charge for just under three years.

Pochettino interviewed for the Man Utd job in March 2022, while Ralf Rangnick was in caretaker charge, and eventually lost out to Erik ten Hag.

Pochettino was set to be sacked by Paris Saint-Germain, despite going on to win the Ligue 1 title that season, after being knocked out of the Champions League by Real Madrid.

#1914. Three Bridges show fighting spirit to earn point against Brentwood Town

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Three Bridges produced a spirited performance on Saturday at Jubilee Field, earning a 1-1 draw against Brentwood Town after an evenly contested encounter. Bridges were desperate to get points on the board, but perhaps even more importantly, to rediscover the battling spirit that had been missing during last week's disappointing performance away at Maldon & Tiptree. Jamie Crellin's men responded positively, showing plenty of fight and determination throughout.

After an even opening, the hosts took the lead in the 12th minute through October's Club Player of the Month, Ade Adeyinka. David Przybylo played Ade through the middle and, from around 20 yards out, he unleashed an unstoppable strike into the net to give Bridges an early advantage.

The remainder of the first half was evenly matched, with Roberts producing several good saves in the Bridges goal. At the other end, the energetic Villavicencio continued to cause problems for the visitors, particularly with a dangerous cross towards Reece Hallard, whose header from six yards narrowly missed the target. Bridges went into the interval holding a deserved 1-0 lead.

It could have been 2-0 just moments into the second half as, straight from the restart, Bridges put together an excellent move down the right. Velvick released Przybylo through on goal, but under pressure from the goalkeeper, his effort narrowly drifted wide.

Brentwood Town began to pile on the pressure at the other end and found their reward in the 58th minute. Following a free-kick from Reid, Gibbs slotted his effort into the bottom corner to restore parity.

Just a couple of minutes later, Przybylo, who had been a constant handful for the visitors, worked his way past his marker and had another opportunity to restore Bridges' advantage, but his effort narrowly missed the far post.

With Bridges short of options on the bench and several players playing through injuries, maintaining the intensity became increasingly difficult. Brentwood Town took control during the final 20 minutes, but Roberts came to the rescue with two superb saves to deny Cerulli and Sears, while the Bridges players continued to put their bodies on the line to protect their point.

There was late drama in the 94th minute when Reece Hallard chased a ball through on the counter-attack, only for Cripps to handle it as the last man. The Brentwood defender was shown a straight red card, leaving the visitors down to ten men. However, it came too late to have any impact on the outcome, as the match finished 1-1.

The point represents a much-needed response from Bridges, who will now face a demanding run of three consecutive away fixtures in seven days. But just two days after their embarrassing FA Cup exit at Wimborne Town, it was another setback for interim boss Kevin Blackwell and his players.

Blackwell made 10 changes from that performance at the weekend against Wimborne. Only Vito Mannone kept his place, and new signing Ayman Benarous started the game, with the other new face Wickham starting on the bench.

In a fairly even first half, both sides played some good flowing football. However, it was the Bees who took the lead on 27 minutes. Omari Mrisho slipped in the penalty area, allowing Luca Picotto to cross, and then a bit of miscommunication between Ben Heneghan and Mannone allowed Bobb-Semple to tap into an empty net at the near post.

It was soon 2-0 when yet another Mrisho error allowed Gustavo Gomez the space to pick out Bobb-Semple to fire home for his second goal of the night. The game settled down a little after that flurry of action.

Rose in the Brentford goal had to make a couple of saves, one from an Aderoju header, and he got a hand to a Klaudio Krasniqi shot, which was possibly going over anyway. Riley Owen fired a shot straight at Mannone midway through the second half.

Crawley’s other new signing, Wickham, managed to open his account for the Reds with a late penalty after Malcolm Ebowei was fouled in the box, to make it 2-1, but it wasn’t enough to put Crawley through.

Man Utd’s interest in the Argentine head coach dates as far back as 2016, with Pochettino even meeting Sir Alex Ferguson for dinner while in charge at Spurs.

In May of this year, Pochettino revealed the Red Devils’ interest was more than just rumours. He told FourFourTwo: “United have always shown interest. But the ideal scenario to manage there has never quite materialised.”

Pochettino went on to state that meeting Sir Alex Ferguson was not a job interview, but instead a younger manager picking the brains of one of the most successful coaches in football history.

He continued: “In any case, that lunch with Sir Alex had absolutely nothing to do with it.

Pochettino interviewed for the manager role at Old Trafford in 2018, losing out to Ole Gunnar Solskjaer.

He explained: “I was under contract at PSG.

“After our Champions League elimination against Real Madrid, we had no option but to make sure we secured the Ligue 1 title at least.

“United were in a hurry to announce their new manager before the end of that season because the situation had become unsustainable. I couldn’t negotiate, whereas Ajax gave Ten Hag the flexibility to do so.”

The former Southampton manager also told L’Equipe earlier this year that he would relish a chance to return to the Premier League.
